a58.speaker: International Monetary Fund (July 2025 Staff Report on Tanzania)
a58.speech: Indicates that over 20,000 Tanzanians working directly and indirectly in the health sector will be affected by the USAID shutdown, and that another 30,000 health workers who received supplemental income through USAID support are also expected to be impacted. "Most foreign assistance cuts have affected the health sector, both supplies and staff. For instance, USAID employed over 20,000 workers, both directly and indirectly (including CSO and community workers), mostly involved in HIV, malaria, family planning, and child health treatments. Another 30,000 health workers were paid by USAID to carry out additional activities beyond their official duties." Highlights that Tanzania was among the largest recipients of USAID support in Sub-Saharan Africa, receiving USD 400 million, equivalent to about 0.5 percent of Tanzania's GDP and about 40 percent of the country's total health expenditure, and estimates that around 0.2 percent of GDP per year in high-priority health spending will be affected by the funding cuts.

a58.speaker: Ministry of Health of Tanzania
a58.speech: According to the Ministry, Tsh 93 billion was allocated to offset the anticipated budget shortfall. Highlighted that it will also restructure some of the roles which were supported by USAID programs to be under direct government budgetary support, in coordination with the President's Office, Public Service Management, and Good Governance.

a58.speaker: Jenista Mhagama, Tanzania's Minister of Health
a58.speech: Told reporters on April 25, 2025, regarding the USAID exit: "Through the coordination of the Prime Minister's Office, we have conducted a comprehensive assessment. We have reviewed what we currently have, what we have ordered, and what we expect to receive. We have already put in place a strategic plan for the short term, medium term, and long term." ; "For malaria medications and diagnostic supplies, we have enough stock to last until February 2026. For other medications, such as HIV drugs and others, we have already taken action. As of now, we have sufficient supplies to last us until June." ; "We have already received funding from the government as part of our short-term plan. We have received 93 billion shillings from the government, and we have already placed orders for medicines for all other diseases that were previously funded by those projects."

a65.speaker: Abdoulaye Maïga, Prime Minister of Mali, Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization
a65.speech: Recalled the eight strategic pillars of government work. Urged members of the new government to adopt the rules, procedures and fundamental principles of government work; the organization and functioning of the General Secretariat of ministerial departments and cabinets; the procedures relating to the declaration of assets of government members; the protocol rules to be observed during government missions; as well as the broad outlines of government action and the Government Action Plan (PAG). Insisted especially on the importance of respecting the fundamental principles that guide government action, namely respect for Mali's sovereignty, the sovereign choices of the people, and the defense of their interests.

a158.speaker: Namibia National Report on Wildlife Protection for 2024 (report)
a158.speech: According to the report, proactive law enforcement has led to the arrest of 855 suspects accused of rhino-related crimes since 2015, when the current rhino poaching crisis first peaked, with 726 rhinos recorded as poached in Namibia by last year; the report notes that the lack of serious consequences for such offences remains a major challenge for rhino conservation and protection in Namibia.

a158.speaker: Namibia National Report on Wildlife Protection for 2024 (report)
a158.speech: “A high number of arrested suspects are known repeat offenders, seasoned criminals with previous arrests related to rhino crimes, out on bail in ongoing court cases, or discharged after being tried” ; “Some suspects have been arrested up to eight times for the past ten years, yet in most scenarios, none of their cases have been finalised” ; the authors warn that many of the arrestees continue to be involved in suspected criminal activities: “Absconding while on bail is not uncommon, with many suspects turning fugitive, and some leaving the country to evade the law.”

a158.speaker: Namibia National Report on Wildlife Protection for 2024 (report)
a158.speech: Recommends that “bail applications should be denied as a preventative measure whenever there is a risk of suspects reoffending, and all means to expedite case finalisation should be employed” ; highlights recidivism as a global challenge in efforts to combat crime: “Recidivism is particularly high amongst Namibian rhino syndicates but is also prevalent in other sectors such as meat poaching” ; “While court cases are ongoing, the suspects are released on bail and are rearrested and charged for similar offences committed while on bail.”

a158.speaker: Namibia National Report on Wildlife Protection for 2024 (report)
a158.speech: Warns that new individuals continue to be drawn into rhino-related crimes, with 61% of suspects arrested in 2024 identified as first-time offenders: “It is vital to demonstrate to such first offenders through swift prosecutions and appropriate sentencing that wildlife crime does not pay” ; says the rhino poaching crisis in Namibia is being compounded by the reality that there are seldom serious consequences for rhino crimes, so that potential illicit gains from rhino poaching and horn trafficking outweigh potential consequences.

a610.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Namibia
a610.speech: Says levels of viral load in nine out of 10 children with the virus are below detection levels.

a610.speaker: Vann Rolfson, Acting Country Representative of USAID
a610.speech: Noted that having nine out of 10 HIV-infected children below the detection level or virally suppressed is another step for Namibia to reach the UN 95-95-95 goals.

a943.speaker: Mozambique and China
a943.speech: expressed, this Monday (26), their interest in strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two countries, particularly in the sectors of trade and industry; both welcomed the excellent state of Sino-Mozambican relations, which has a visible impact on the continued strengthening of political, economic and social exchange.

a943.speaker: Maria Lucas, Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
a943.speech: praised the growth in political and diplomatic cooperation, which has been reflected in the exchange of visits at different levels, especially presidential visits ; “We will continue to work, as we have already said, but just to say that this year we are celebrating 50 years of Mozambique's independence” ; “We will have a celebration here in Maputo, but there will also be a big celebration in China” ; said that the Mozambican president, Daniel Chapo, was already preparing for his visit to China in 2026 ; “So, there is plenty to celebrate, and that is why your coming here, your arrival here, is very welcome by the government, by the party, but also by the Mozambican people.”

a943.speaker: Maria Lucas, Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
a943.speech: acknowledged the continued support that China has provided to Mozambique in various sectors, with emphasis on the areas of humanitarian assistance, food security and infrastructure, and thanked the Chinese representative for the support provided for the materialization of the President of the Republic's Plan for the First 100 Days of Governance ; “His Excellency President Daniel Chapo asked me to welcome our Special Representative to Mozambique and also to inform him that he is visiting the province of Gaza and also to inform him that his 100-day plan was successful because of the support that China gave” ; “In addition to the support that China gave, in relation to financial support for various areas of humanitarian aid, we also laid the foundation stone for the construction of the Mozambique Surgical Centre, which will be the largest in Mozambique.”

a947.speaker: Majority of Lagos State House of Assembly members
a947.speech: have affirmed that the impeachment of former Speaker Hon. Mudashiru Obasa adhered to due process.

a947.speaker: Justice Yetunde Pinheiro, Lagos High Court (court record)
a947.speech: adjourned the suit filed by Obasa challenging his impeachment and has scheduled March 7, 2025, to hear multiple applications submitted by various counsels involved in the case.

a947.speaker: Hon. Ogundipe Stephen Olukayode, Lagos State House of Assembly member speaking on behalf of the lawmakers supporting Speaker Meranda
a947.speech: “We have made our position clear, and in due time, the truth will be revealed for everyone to see.”

a947.speaker: Hon. Ogundipe Stephen Olukayode, Lagos State House of Assembly member
a947.speech: Addressing the controversial sitting held by Obasa in the House on Thursday: “We are very clear on this matter. Let me also take this opportunity to appreciate the press for standing with what is right. You all saw what happened there—it was a show of shame. Even when questions were raised, the responses given were neither logical nor in line with legal procedures.” ; “How could he claim to still be Speaker when the court proceedings are ongoing? He was the one who took the matter to court in the first place. And yet, you saw the drama, even from his lawyers. It is very unfortunate. But when we get to the bridge, we will cross it.”

a947.speaker: Hon. Ogundipe Stephen Olukayode, Lagos State House of Assembly member
a947.speech: When asked about the number of Assembly members supporting Speaker Meranda, confidently stated, “As we speak, we are 35.”

a947.speaker: Hon. Ogundipe Stephen Olukayode, Lagos State House of Assembly member
a947.speech: Speaking on Obasa's alleged forceful entry into the Speaker's office and the Assembly chambers on Thursday: “I won't speak on behalf of the party, but I know that the party is taking necessary steps in response. We are consulting with our leaders, and all rightful actions will be taken.” ; “But let me assure Lagosians that we remain committed to our party, our leadership, and, most importantly, to serving the people of Lagos State. That is our primary concern. We are law-abiding lawmakers, and we are handling everything within our power in a responsible manner.” ; When asked what action would be taken if a similar incident occurred again, he responded, “We pray it does not happen again.”

a947.speaker: Hon. Ogundipe Stephen Olukayode, Lagos State House of Assembly member
a947.speech: On the official position of the House, reaffirmed: “Madam Speaker has spoken. The House will reconvene at the appropriate time. When it is time, we will be invited, and all necessary procedures will be followed accordingly.”

a947.speaker: Sahara Reporters (@SaharaReporters) social media post
a947.speech: “WATCH: 35 Lagos Assembly Lawmakers Insist Obasa's Impeachment Followed Due Process” — posted February 28, 2025.

a1038.speaker: Bank of Abyssinia (BoA) statement
a1038.speech: indicated that in the 2016/2017 fiscal year the number of depositors stood at 750,000, while it has now increased by 35 percent and reached more than one million.

a1038.speaker: Bank of Abyssinia (BoA) financial report
a1038.speech: indicated that the proportion of loans showed term loans took the lion's share by 66 percent and over draft and advances stood at 21.3 and 12 percent respectively; that the bank mobilized USD 382 million, a decline of 10 percent compared with 2016/17, with declines in incoming transfers, money transfers, and interest on corresponding banks; and that mobile banking users doubled and the card banking service grew by 83 percent.

a1262.speaker: Standard Bank Plc (Malawi)
a1262.speech: Has welcomed the new administration's commitment to restoring economic stability, predictability, and strong governance, describing the move as a critical step toward rebuilding investor confidence and national growth.

a1262.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive Officer
a1262.speech: Said the bank is ready to work hand in hand with government and other key stakeholders to help implement President Arthur Peter Mutharika's plan to tackle the country's pressing macroeconomic challenges. ; "Attracting foreign direct investment from key economies such as the United States and China, as outlined in President Mutharika's inauguration speech, is crucial to unlocking Malawi's growth potential and achieving meaningful recovery," Madinga said.

a1262.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive Officer
a1262.speech: Commended the President's determination to renew diplomatic relations with the United States, saying his special friendship with U.S. President Donald Trump could pave the way for stronger economic and trade ties. ; "Easing diplomatic hurdles with the U.S. should set the stage for dialogue aimed at finding lasting solutions for Malawi's economy, trade, and diplomatic relations," he added.

a1262.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive Officer
a1262.speech: Noted that the loss of development and technical assistance following USAID's departure had negatively affected the country, emphasizing the need for renewed engagement and open dialogue to explore sustainable solutions.

a1262.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive Officer
a1262.speech: Further highlighted the importance of a strong public-private partnership during the next three months of the government's transition period, describing it as a crucial window to re-set the country's economic trajectory. ; "Malawi must now reaffirm its resolve to restore stability through fiscal discipline, good governance, and meaningful dialogue with bilateral and multilateral donors and creditors. The foundation for a stronger, more resilient economy must be laid now," Madinga concluded.

a1485.speaker: Action-research study conducted in Benin in July 2015 (Beninese Association of Constitutional Law project supported by OSIWA)
a1485.speech: Proposes as its main measures prioritising prevention of the drug phenomenon through greater emphasis on grassroots education, rethinking the treatment and social reintegration of drug addicts by incorporating traditional medicine, and revisiting the legal bases of law enforcement by adapting them to current realities. The action-research outlines strategic measures taking into account the whole anti-drug system and placing people back at the heart of the solution. It finds that so-called hard drugs — Indian hemp, cocaine, methamphetamines, heroin and, to a certain extent, tramadol — continue to transit through Beninese villages and towns, that cannabis is produced locally in the departments of Atacora, Donga, Collines and Ouémé-Plateau, and that Benin is both an importer and a supplier of Indian hemp to neighbouring countries.

a1485.speaker: United States Department of State report dated 4 March 2002
a1485.speech: Considered Benin a transit zone for narcotics in West Africa; thirteen years later the situation has not changed at all and, on the contrary, the target group for drugs has widened in Benin.

a1485.speaker: Central Office for the Repression of Illicit Drug and Precursor Trafficking (OCERTID)
a1485.speech: From 2011 to 2014 it seized 58,013.302 kilograms of drugs of all categories combined.

a1504.speaker: Hafeni Ndemula, Deputy Minister of Labour, Industrialization and Employment Creation of Namibia
a1504.speech: has urged all employers to review workers' wages annually. Speaking at the commencement of Labour Day in Swakopmund, he pointed out that some employers are still paying workers below the minimum wage and said that after 33 years of independence, some workers are still subjected to unfair labour practises. "We are dealing with the problem of unemployment that is threatening the future of the youth. It is regrettable to say that there are still employers who opt to operate with labour standards, and some do not pay their employees their minimum wages." ; He called on those still unemployed to use their skills for self-employment.

a1504.speaker: Neville Andre, Erongo Governor
a1504.speech: said COVID-19 highlighted the significance of workers in different categories and their role in economic revival, and applauded trade unions for standing by the workers in the midst of difficult times. "Workers and trade unions are at the heart of our country's economy; it is you who mine the minerals and introduce exports that fuel our growth. It is you who put the food on our table and bear the facilities that deliver the services our people need, and without your organised participation, our efforts to become more productive and comparative will not succeed. Employees have the talent to reshape our economy."

a1609.speaker: Dr Jane Ruth Aceng Ocero, Uganda's Minister of Health
a1609.speech: "This outbreak tested our resilience, but through swift coordination and a unified response, we were able to overcome the crisis."

a1609.speaker: Dr Charles Njuguna, WHO Representative in Uganda
a1609.speech: Noted, on the mobilisation of vaccine candidates for Sudan ebolavirus: "The speed at which we mobilized and deployed resources, including experimental vaccines, was a testament to the progress we have made in global health security."

a1609.speaker: Moses Muyenga, Ebola survivor and community advocate
a1609.speech: "Our battle did not end with my recovery. I want to ensure no one else suffers from the same stigma we faced."

a1609.speaker: Dr Moeti Matshidiso, WHO Regional Director
a1609.speech: Emphasized, on regional readiness assessments and trainings in neighbouring countries: "It's crucial to build not only national but also regional capacity, so we are prepared for any future outbreaks."

a1609.speaker: Dr Charles Njuguna, WHO Representative in Uganda
a1609.speech: Concluded: "This outbreak showed us the importance of preparation, coordination, and community involvement in tackling global health crises."

a1611.speaker: Insurance and Pensions Commission (Ipec) of Zimbabwe
a1611.speech: Has said Zimbabwe's short-term insurers grew revenue by 30 percent in the first half of 2025 to ZiG3,72 billion, driven mainly by motor and fire insurance policies.

a2000.speaker: US State Department
a2000.speech: Made public on 4 August a pilot project under which certain foreigners will have to pay a bond of up to fifteen thousand US dollars for an entry visa to the United States; the arrangement, scheduled to be tested from 20 August and to last twelve months, targets holders of B-1 and B-2 visas from countries where visa overstay rates are judged to be high, and concerns both business and tourist visas.

a2000.speaker: US Government
a2000.speech: According to the American government, for the year 2023 alone no fewer than half a million people are suspected of having fallen foul of the law by remaining in the United States beyond the authorised duration of their stay.

a2000.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a2000.speech: Is determined to restore to his country “its former greatness”, having made the fight against illegal immigration one of the priorities of his current term.

a2409.speaker: Residents of the Kabaase displacement camp near Doolow
a2409.speech: Citing extreme food shortages, lack of healthcare, and growing despair due to aid suspensions and worsening security conditions ; say conditions in the camp have deteriorated further following recent political tensions and international funding cuts ; are now calling on both the Somali government and the international community to restore aid flows and establish long-term resettlement and recovery plans.

a2409.speaker: Yarow Isaaq Iman, 52, displaced man who fled to the camp in 2011
a2409.speech: Described the situation as “hopeless,” saying displaced families are stuck in dire poverty with no access to employment or basic services. “There are no jobs, no development — the general situation is very bad,” Yarow told Kaab TV.

a2409.speaker: United Nations
a2409.speech: According to the United Nations, more than 3.8 million people are currently displaced within the country, driven by conflict, drought, and insecurity.

a2409.speaker: Magaalo Aadan Ali, 38, camp resident
a2409.speech: Said the Federal Government’s decision to suspend domestic flights to Doolow — amid a dispute with the Jubaland administration — has deepened the isolation of vulnerable communities. “The situation worsened after the U.S. government cut humanitarian aid, particularly assistance from USAID. We are in urgent need of help. Young people here have no income or opportunities.” ; “We don’t just need emergency food. We need lasting solutions — a future.”

a2409.speaker: Ali Ibrahim Ahmed, 43, who fled from the Bakool region in 2016
a2409.speech: Said he has not received any aid in four years. “When the U.S. pulled its support, food shortages became even more severe.”

a2409.speaker: Aid workers and community leaders
a2409.speech: Report growing concerns over malnutrition, especially among children.

a2409.speaker: Yarow Isaaq Iman, 52, displaced man in Kabaase camp
a2409.speech: Noted that many school-aged children have been forced to drop out due to hunger. “Even children who used to attend school have returned home — they’re too hungry to continue learning. There’s no food at all.”

a2632.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (session of 3 April)
a2632.speech: Adopted a draft decree determining the conditions for carrying out transit activities for dangerous or strategic materials as well as equipment and materiel departing from or destined for Burkina.

a2801.speaker: Management of Realnews Magazine and Publications Limited
a2801.speech: has announced that Honourable Justice Ayotunde Phillips will chair the Realnews 13th Anniversary Lecture.

a2801.speaker: Justice Ayotunde Phillips, former Chief Judge of Lagos State
a2801.speech: Her acceptance to Chair the lecture was communicated to Realnews in her message on September 22, 2025, stating: "It is my honour to chair such a distinguished event."

a2844.speaker: Tesfalem Bekele, resident of Amibara Wereda, Afar Regional State, whose home was submerged
a2844.speech: "That's what comes with living here. We were standing guard this year when it happened." ; "We left with the clothes on our back."

a2844.speaker: Tesfalem Bekele, resident of Amibara Wereda, Afar Regional State
a2844.speech: "The man had over 6,000ha, so he helped us out with irrigating our land. We also work on his farm."

a2844.speaker: Tesfalem Bekele, resident of Amibara Wereda, Afar Regional State
a2844.speech: said the bulldozers in Amibara working to close off the river and return it to its right track only appear once the rain starts to drop: "Flood risks are not new to us. It happens every year. But every year the government comes a little too late."

a2844.speaker: National Meteorological Agency of Ethiopia
a2844.speech: issued a warning earlier in August which predicted unusually heavy and continuous rainfall across the country.

a2844.speaker: National Disaster & Risk Management Commission (Flood Emergency Response Plan)
a2844.speech: The Flood Response Plan crafted by the Commission has estimated that close to half a million people have food assistance, but over half a million more new beneficiaries are anticipated.

a2844.speaker: Abiye Abdu, community representative in charge of receiving and distributing supplies at the Amibara campsite
a2844.speech: "There's some clothes and other items in there. But we haven't been told to distribute it." ; "We need food and water. What're we going to do with sanitiser?"

a2844.speaker: Amina Yasin, displaced mother of seven living in a classroom campsite in Asaita
a2844.speech: "We were taken out by a helicopter. There was no way to leave our houses as the water was quick." ; "I don't know how I can restart my life with nothing."

a2844.speaker: Mohammad Husen, director of the Afar Disaster Prevention & Food Security Coordination Office
a2844.speech: said the floods have caused the destruction of 21,000 sheep, goats and camels in the region: "There is a recovery and rehabilitation plan underway, and this involves restocking families with cattle and facilitating a permanent home," to be implemented in a three to six-month plan that will also include mending parts of the 300Km of damaged roads in the region.

a2844.speaker: Mohammad Husen, director of the Afar Disaster Prevention & Food Security Coordination Office
a2844.speech: "This is rainfall that we haven't seen in over 30 years. It is beyond our capacity to address it, so we had to request support from the Federal government." ; said the regional Bureau has all the names and lists of the displaced people and that the report shows no lives have been lost.

a2844.speaker: Hassen Ahmed, displaced resident of a campsite in Amibara
a2844.speech: "We weren't relocated together. We can't tell who has been rescued and who hasn't. We've been separated."

a2844.speaker: UNICEF (assessment)
a2844.speech: marked the inaccessible area of Amibara in Zone 03 as a priority zone; supplies of buckets, water treatment kits, storage tanks and jerrycans have been dispatched at a cost of 50,000 dollars to Amibara and five other weredas, and the organisation expects to receive an additional 70,000 dollars for rehabilitating and maintaining damaged and non-functional water schemes from the UN's Central Emergency Relief Fund; according to the organisation's assessment, gaps still exist in water and non-food item provisions among others.

a2844.speaker: Muluneh Woldetsadik (PhD), expert in geography and environment
a2844.speech: said ill preparation may be one of the culprits for this crisis, as floods of this nature seldom occur: "The topography of the affected areas is another factor, as it is a lowland area that collects all the water that has nowhere else to go." ; "The amount of rainfall dropping within a short amount of time is quite high, and that has affected the water retention capabilities of the ground." ; recommended that resettlement of people living in these high-risk areas is one approach to ensure future risk mitigation, and that working on dikes and water canals that can help minimise the impact of floods should also be done in a very critical manner.

a3225.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a3225.speech: "Peace be with you" were his first words on the day he was elected as the new head of the Catholic Church (8 May), addressing the faithful in St Peter's Square ; three days later, at his first Sunday greeting to pilgrims, he cried "never again war," speaking "to the great ones of the world" and referring to the "current dramatic scenario of a Third World War in pieces."

a3225.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a3225.speech: Evoking the "sufferings of the beloved people" of Ukraine, asked that "everything possible be done to achieve as quickly as possible an authentic, just and lasting peace" in the country at war ; noted during the Mass inaugurating his pontificate that "martyred Ukraine" awaits "negotiations for a just and lasting peace."

a3225.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a3225.speech: "I am deeply saddened by what is happening in the Gaza Strip," calling for an "immediate ceasefire" and "humanitarian aid" for "the exhausted civilian population," as well as "that all hostages be released" ; during the Mass inaugurating his pontificate warned of the hunger suffered in Gaza by "children, families and the elderly" and asked for humanitarian aid.

a3225.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a3225.speech: At an audience with representatives of the 23 Eastern Catholic Churches, urged world leaders to sit down and negotiate in order to "silence the weapons," and offered the Vatican's mediation to all the warring parties.

a3225.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a3225.speech: On the occasion of the 80th anniversary of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, said he hoped their memory would "serve as a universal warning against the devastation caused by war, and in particular by nuclear weapons."

a3225.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a3225.speech: Appealed several times to world leaders not to ignore the needs of the most vulnerable, proposing at the Mass inaugurating his Pontificate a Catholic Church united against "an economic paradigm that exploits the Earth's resources and marginalises the poorest" ; criticised "imbalances and injustices that lead (...) to undignified working conditions and to increasingly fragmented and conflict-ridden societies" ; asked for "efforts to remedy global inequalities, which leave deep gulfs between opulence and poverty, between continents, countries and even within societies," considering that "good political action, which favours an equitable distribution of resources, can offer an effective service to harmony and peace, both at the social and international level" ; defended the preservation of the dignity of migrants and encouraged more than a million pilgrims gathered in Rome for the Jubilee of Young People to "aspire to great things" and not to fall into conformism and materialism.

a3225.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a3225.speech: On abuse, stated that there must be no tolerance in the Catholic Church for any kind of abuse, whether sexual, spiritual or of authority, and defended a culture of prevention based on "active vigilance, (...) transparent processes and (...) a sincere listening to those who have been wounded."

a3225.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a3225.speech: Called for "a renewed dialogue" on how the future of the planet is being built, in a message marking the 10th anniversary of Francis's encyclical "Laudato Si" for the protection of the "common home that God entrusted to us."

a3225.speaker: Geraldo Alckmin, Vice-President of Brazil
a3225.speech: According to the vice-president of Brazil, Leo XIV received "with great sympathy" his government's invitation to take part in the Climate Summit (COP30) in November, in the Amazonian city of Belem.

a3225.speaker: Antonio Marto, Portuguese cardinal
a3225.speech: According to the Portuguese cardinal, the Pope also thanked the invitation to visit the Sanctuary of Fatima, after having been twice in Portugal when he went only by the name Robert Prevost.

a3300.speaker: Addis Abeba City Administration
a3300.speech: Said the assistance, received by Deputy Mayor Takele Uma, will directly go through as cash support to sustain the households for three months.

a3304.speaker: Kondwani Msimuko, Illovo Sugar acting Managing Director
a3304.speech: Addressing shareholders on Friday, cited the drop in profitability to economic woes Malawi was facing, singling out foreign currency scarcity, high taxes, vandalism and other macroeconomic uncertainties among the challenges: "We had lower profits last year, and our intention for this meeting was actually to get to our investors and update them on the company's performance, factors behind it and what we are doing to improve [the situation] moving forward."

a3304.speaker: Kondwani Msimuko, Illovo Sugar acting Managing Director
a3304.speech: Assured investors that the company was making strides to improve revenue generation through increased production and export of products.

a3304.speaker: Maureen Kachingwe, Illovo Sugar Director of Legal and Corporate Affairs
a3304.speech: In her presentation, said the company spent about K2.13 billion towards supporting community development activities through their response to natural disasters and fulfilment of corporate social responsibility roles.

a3304.speaker: Frank Harawa, shareholder
a3304.speech: Said they were concerned about the company's low profit; was quick to commend management for its efforts amid a challenging operating environment.

a3344.speaker: Brook Taye (PhD), former director general of the Ethiopian Capital Market Authority (ECMA) and former advisor to the Ministry of Finance (policy recommendation)
a3344.speech: Submitted a comprehensive policy recommendation urging a review of the existing corporate tax structure to stimulate market growth; conducted a detailed study to identify tax policy alternatives that could kickstart the emerging capital market.

a3344.speaker: Brook Taye (PhD), CEO of the Ethiopian Investment Holdings and former ECMA director general
a3344.speech: At a high-profile event hosted by MTA Law Firm at Skylight Hotel last week, exuded confidence about the upcoming market, slated for operations in November with Ethio telecom offering 10pc of its shares to the public.

a3344.speaker: Estifanos Melkamu, head of the licensing and registration directorate at ECMA
a3344.speech: "The objective is to create an enabling environment in the financial market"; believes establishing an enabling environment and encouraging market development are crucial for the capital market's successful operation; cautioned that the existing tax laws are not adequately supportive and could impede the market's efficient operations. ; "Certain regulations could pose challenges in the capital market operation."

a3344.speaker: Abraham Arega, tax policy advisor at the Ministry of Finance
a3344.speech: Acknowledged the necessity of overhauling the current tax regime, which has overlooked the capital market's operations; disclosed that the detailed fiscal consequences are yet to be fully understood due to ongoing studies. ; "Revenue implications need to be thoroughly considered"; said the Ministry is developing a "broadly applicable, fair, and effective" income tax system to improve the overall tax structure. ; "While various suggestions for reviews have been proposed, the potential consequences are under evaluation," stating that tax reductions are on the table, while no tax exemptions are being considered.

a3344.speaker: Individuals following the progress (anonymous)
a3344.speech: Said an overhaul is underway, revising the income tax structure and identifying loopholes needing reform.

a3344.speaker: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) research
a3344.speech: Found that tax laws often reflect financial needs or policy goals inconsistent with or neglectful of financial market development objectives, and that financial market tax laws have often evolved without assessing their impact on these markets.

a3344.speaker: Worku Lemma, senior banker
a3344.speech: Observed banks hesitant to participate more proactively in the market as they carefully watch potential gains and risks. ; "Banks are widely expected to contribute immensely to the growth of the capital market. But, they're dragging their feet." ; Said banks play a crucial role in making the capital market successful, given their resource mobilisation and edge in familiarity and expertise with the capital and money markets; found it puzzling that banks, many of which have already invested in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX), are indecisive about fully participating. ; "Considering their expected role in driving market growth, it's baffling to see them remain on the sidelines."

a3344.speaker: Kassahun Tilahun, CEO of the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX)
a3344.speech: Would like to see tax incentives offered for companies, especially those listed on the Exchange, and is advocating for reviews of the capital gains tax for listed public companies. ; "Such incentives will encourage many companies to be listed"; argued that companies with limited liability might continue to operate under the existing tax regime, potentially incentivising them to consider public listing to benefit from more favourable tax treatment; believes these incentives would encourage investors to put their equity in listed companies, noting that regional experiences show such initiatives have been adopted elsewhere.

a3344.speaker: Mered B. Fikireyohannes, finance and investment advisor
a3344.speech: Sees existing tax laws restraining diversification in investment, prodding many to focus solely on property investments. ; "The existing laws have to be properly examined"; would like to see the tax regime supporting transaction and trading activities; advocated for tax policies that eliminate double taxation of collective investment schemes. ; "Being listed is a huge burden in itself. Given the long-term nature of capital market savings and investments, changes to the tax laws could substantially impact the country's fiscal and economic well-being." ; Said tax laws should be revised to remove obstacles to the capital market's development. ; "The tax regime has to encourage long-term saving and investments."

a3344.speaker: Industry experts
a3344.speech: Caution that without a supportive tax environment, the capital market may struggle to attract participation from domestic and foreign investors.

a3429.speaker: Monica Chakwera, First Lady of Malawi
a3429.speech: Appealed for increased domestic financial support in the fight against tuberculosis, emphasising the urgent need for sustainable local funding towards TB prevention and treatment services: "Collectively, we need to act with urgency and commitment, investing in resources that can help end TB come 2030. This will require the private sector and other stakeholders domestically mobilise funds."

a3429.speaker: Monica Chakwera, First Lady of Malawi
a3429.speech: Highlighted progress by Malawi in the fight against TB under the Leprosy and Tuberculosis programme, including the integration of HIV and Aids with TB treatment, which she said has been crucial: "Reduced mortality rates which is currently at 54 percent among HIV-negative individuals and 60 percent HIV-positive individuals and high treatment success rates are signs we are doing well in the fight against TB. We need to intensify efforts to completely end the disease."

a3429.speaker: Monica Chakwera, First Lady of Malawi
a3429.speech: Said the fight is far from over and requires concerted efforts from various sectors to eliminate the disease's burden, observing that the fight against TB cannot be won by the health sector alone; urged players in different sectors, including high risk industries such as mining and tobacco, to work together, and urged the youth, women and other stakeholders to be at the forefront in the fight against the disease, which affects 12 percent of the Malawi population, mainly children and adolescents.

a3429.speaker: Noah Chimpeni, Deputy Minister of Health of Malawi
a3429.speech: Said the ministry is working on increasing domestic resource mobilisation as one way of addressing the heavy reliance on external funding, which accounts for 64 percent of total health expenditures: "The emphasis on self-reliance is key to long-term sustainability of health care, as such there is need to improve efficiency in health care spending and look at areas, including costly referrals outside Malawi."

a3429.speaker: Edna Tembo, executive director, Coalition of Women Living with HIV in Malawi
a3429.speech: Said the recent suspension of US foreign aid will significantly impact efforts in the fight against TB and other diseases, and therefore called on government and the private sector to respond collectively to the changes, which have caused a major setback.

a3437.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a3437.speech: Disclosed that the services sector is expected to account for 38% of GDP, followed by agriculture and fisheries at 29%, with mining and panning contributing 19.2%, forestry about 8%, and manufacturing 6%; emphasised the services sector's resilience and potential for further growth ; "The services sector remains a key driver of our economy, contributing significantly to job creation and income generation... We aim to further strengthen this sector by improving infrastructure, access to credit, and policy frameworks that encourage investment."

a3437.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a3437.speech: "Agriculture is not just a source of food; it is the backbone of our economy and a lifeline for our people. Through strategic partnerships and increased funding, we are equipping farmers with tools, training, and market access to maximize productivity."

a3437.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a3437.speech: On mining: "We recognize the mining sector's potential to catalyze development, but we must balance growth with sustainability. Our focus is on ensuring that revenues from mining are transparently managed and reinvested into communities."

a3437.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a3437.speech: On manufacturing: "We are creating an enabling environment for the manufacturing sector by improving energy access and reducing barriers to investment. The goal is to add value to our raw materials locally and create more jobs."

a3437.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a3437.speech: Highlighted that the projected GDP composition is a testament to the effectiveness of ongoing reforms and investments: "This is a balanced and forward-looking economic strategy. By focusing on sectors with high growth potential, we are laying the foundation for sustained development and resilience." ; "This is not just about numbers; it's about changing lives... Together, we can build a resilient, inclusive, and prosperous Liberia."

a3437.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a3437.speech: On partnerships: "We cannot achieve this alone. The private sector and our development partners are essential allies in this journey toward shared prosperity."

a3437.speaker: Samuel Tweah (former Liberian finance minister)
a3437.speech: Noted that public investment projects under the ARREST agenda would further boost economic activity across sectors.

a3437.speaker: Development partners, including the World Bank, African Development Bank, and USAID
a3437.speech: Have pledged support for Liberia's economic transformation.

a3483.speaker: High Powered Exploration (HPX)
a3483.speech: Has spent years masquerading as a champion of Liberian development, claiming its sole interest is to transport iron ore from Guinea via the Buchanan-Yekepa rail.

a3483.speaker: High Powered Exploration (HPX)
a3483.speech: For five years, they've insisted AML cannot remain the rail operator - despite AML's proven track record of safe, transparent operations in Liberia ; claims Liberia alone must appoint an "independent operator" by 2030.

a3483.speaker: High Powered Exploration (HPX)
a3483.speech: Has peddled the false narrative that the U.S. government demands Liberia appoint an "independent operator" or risk losing Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) funds.

a3584.speaker: Sara Beysolow Nyanti, Liberian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3584.speech: argued in favour of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's support for Liberia's candidacy for a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, while calling for a strengthening of bilateral cooperation in the areas of development ; recalled Liberia's commitment to international peace and security, underlining the importance of Saudi support for her country's candidacy to the UN Security Council.

a3584.speaker: Sara Beysolow Nyanti, Liberian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3584.speech: expressed Liberia's gratitude for the historic ties that bind the two countries, and welcomed the Kingdom's constant support, notably towards the Liberian Muslim community through the granting of pilgrimage places in Mecca ; thanked the Saudi government for two recent forms of support: a donation of two million dollars intended for the renovation of the Liberian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and humanitarian aid comprising 500,000 dollars in foodstuffs and 50 tonnes of dates.

a3584.speaker: Sara Beysolow Nyanti, Liberian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3584.speech: highlighted the country's urgent needs for foreign investment, notably in the agriculture, infrastructure and energy sectors, and urged the Saudi authorities to deepen bilateral cooperation in order to contribute to Liberia's economic recovery.

a3584.speaker: Joseph Nyumah Boakai, President of Liberia (message conveyed by the Foreign Minister)
a3584.speech: expressed his wish to strengthen economic, technical and cultural ties with the Kingdom.

a3584.speaker: Waleed A. Elkhereiji, Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3584.speech: praised Liberia's political stability, commending the peaceful transition of power following the last elections; reaffirmed Riyadh's support for the Liberian candidacy to the Security Council and undertook to deepen cooperation in priority development areas.

a3595.speaker: Roads Directorate
a3595.speech: has said the road reserve is encroached by doing the following within the road margins without obtaining approval from the Roads Directorate: constructing a building, erecting a fence, making a ditch or dike or any other thing, planting trees, placing anything, leaving or keeping any structure on the road whether resting on wheels or in any manner.

a3595.speaker: Affected street vendors of Ha Tsolo Usave area (anonymous)
a3595.speech: said they have had running meetings with the directorate to save their businesses, but with no clear decision arrived at on whether the removals will go ahead as scheduled. They said they were told to move on their own by February 21, or matters will take a nasty turn. The vendors indicated that they had asked for a meeting before the given deadline, the meeting failed to materialize and no decision was taken on whether the removals would continue by as scheduled. ; “What we believe is that, this is a specific fight against vendors in this area. There are many businesses here which we think they will not remove, it looks like it is just us,” they said. ; “We did comply. We are not in any way hindering movement where we are situated. There was a reconstruction of the road from the Thetsane Circle and yet the vendors were not asked to move. Why is it not the same with us?” they rhetorically asked.

a3595.speaker: Affected street vendors of Ha Tsolo Usave area (anonymous)
a3595.speech: allege that when they sought permission for establishing their small life sustaining businesses, they followed legal procedures to situate their shacks along the road — they talked to the area chief who listed their names down and then sent it to the Maseru City Council (MCC) for review. They claim they were later granted permission to erect their shacks a distance away from the road so that when the directorate makes pavements it would not distort the whole process.

a3595.speaker: Kamohelo Makojoa, vendor
a3595.speech: shared that they were also told to move and lucky for him he was able to find space for relocation, others not so lucky. Makojoa said they were recently shown where the road reserve actually supposed to be. ; “We were told to move 15 metres from the centre of the road, not just us but solid buildings along the road, some reputable businesses, are said to have encroached on the road reserve. They will have to move. Not only that, but Usave packing lot will also be affected,” said Makojoa.

a3595.speaker: Teboho Mokhoane, Director General of the Roads Directorate
a3595.speech: said they had made guidelines, engaged internal and external stakeholders, held community gatherings beforehand as well as public awareness and have also engaged the media. He noted that now they are at the state where they are making enforcement to avoid encroachment of the road reserve. ; “We are on the journey of removing those that are already where we have resumed work . . . if we find anyone fixing their car in the road or anyone building a shack we will have to solve that matter immediately,” he said. ; He mentioned that they are already in talks with those that seem to have built permanent structures along the road reserve. He said they are doing this in alignment with the Roads Act of 1969 and the Roads Directorate Act of 2010 which highlight the meaning of a road reserve.

a3595.speaker: Nozesolo Mpopo, Roads Directorate Manager Corporate Communications
a3595.speech: detailed in an interview with this reporter that the only way the public could stop encroaching on the road reserve is by having clear and visible demarcated road reserves with installation of road reserve markers, regular monitoring (road reserve patrol) and enforcement actions (transgression notices etc.). She noted that community awareness campaigns, stricter regulations, review of the Road Act of 1969, strengthening collaboration with local authorities, enforcement with the Lesotho Mounted Police Services (LMPS), utilizing Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping to identify encroachments for database and monitoring purposes as well as strengthening collaboration with the Land Administration Authority (LAA) could go a long way in saving both the Directorate and financially pitiable vendors.

a3595.speaker: Nozesolo Mpopo, Roads Directorate Manager Corporate Communications
a3595.speech: “Roads Directorate does not issue leases. Councils and the LAA do this function. There are working arrangements per case with LAA to provide lease boundary maps and Roads Directorate road reserve approval for lease applications, there is also a construction permit committee of RD with MCC and other stakeholders; LEC, WASCO, Energy etc.,” said Mpopo. ; “There are district community development committees which comprises the DA, Councils, economic planners, business representatives to mention a few at districts to which cases of encroachment in developments are adjudicated,” she said, further noting Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) are being developed for formal working agreements.

a3595.speaker: Nozesolo Mpopo, Roads Directorate Manager Corporate Communications
a3595.speech: indicated that the suspension of applications for new businesses was for Maseru district applications only at the time, adding that the purpose of the suspension of applications for access was to enhance traffic flow, lower traffic accidents and to slow down the rate of encroachments into the road reserve. ; “The suspension was prompted by amongst others the following; the current design guidelines prohibiting access within a space of 500m (minimum) and 600m (maximum) respectively depending on factors of the land available, increased level of traffic disruptions by traffic trails into businesses disrupting traffic flows,” she said. She further mentioned that high level of encroachment by businesses causing loading and off-loading in the road reserve disrupting traffic flows was another cause.

a3595.speaker: Nozesolo Mpopo, Roads Directorate Manager Corporate Communications
a3595.speech: “The Roads Act of 1969 outlines offences in the road reserve, encroachment is one of the activities listed as offences in the Act necessitating RD to enforce compliance with the law.”

a3595.speaker: Nozesolo Mpopo, Roads Directorate Manager Corporate Communications
a3595.speech: said her department doesn’t always act swiftly upon expiry of a deadline. “We give people time to comply, until such time that we will be forced to remove them ourselves,” Mpopo said.

a3734.speaker: Black Sherif, Ghanaian musician
a3734.speech: “IRON BOY is where peak optimism and anxiety meet the notion of perseverance and stealth, all coming together to build a self-supporting frame. Somewhere along the line, I got obsessed with my aspirations of getting the people to not see me past an art maker who got noticed. I couldn’t make it happen, so I let it be. A sudden need to feel grounded came to shake up my whole frame, and so, I plan to build harmony between every line of my thinking” ; “This album is for everyone finding their way, embracing their truth, and pushing against the odds.”

a3917.speaker: Maria Hamunyela, registered nurse with the Walvis Bay Corridor Group (WBCG)
a3917.speech: Said mobile populations, including long-distance truck drivers, female sex workers as well as men who have sex with other men, continue to pose unique challenges to health service delivery in the Erongo Region: “Our biggest challenge is following up with mobile populations. Truck drivers travel long distances, sometimes crossing borders, and female sex workers often relocate, making continuity of care difficult.”

a3917.speaker: Maria Hamunyela, registered nurse with the Walvis Bay Corridor Group (WBCG)
a3917.speech: Highlighted persistent stigma and misconceptions about pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which discourage high-risk populations from accessing vital HIV prevention services.

a3917.speaker: Maria Hamunyela, registered nurse with the Walvis Bay Corridor Group (WBCG)
a3917.speech: Stressed that budget constraints, worsened by the withdrawal of USAID support, have severely affected clinic operations: “In the past, we could visit smaller towns frequently, but now outreach to places like Usakos, Omaruru and Karibib is minimal compared to before” ; added that limited resources mean mobile clinics cannot cover as much ground as required, leaving high-risk populations underserved.

a3917.speaker: Maria Hamunyela, registered nurse with the Walvis Bay Corridor Group (WBCG)
a3917.speech: Recommended strengthening community engagement to reduce stigma, improving client tracking systems, and expanding both mobile and static health services.

a3958.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP), 2024 edition of its biennial report on the state of school feeding worldwide
a3958.speech: According to the report, twenty million more children in sub-Saharan Africa receive school meals compared with 2022, the region recording the strongest progress: from 66 million children served in 2022 to 87 million in 2024, an increase of more than 30%; Benin, alongside Botswana, Burkina Faso, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, Rwanda and Zambia, is among the countries financing their programmes mainly from national budgets; in Benin direct purchases from smallholder farmers jumped by 800% in two years, benefiting more than 23,000 producers ; the report indicates that countries such as Chad, Ethiopia, Madagascar and Rwanda have multiplied by six the number of pupils receiving school meals since 2022, that in Burundi local sourcing increased farmers' incomes by 50% and created jobs in 67 cooperatives, and that in Malawi every dollar invested in school meals generates eight dollars in economic benefits.

a3958.speaker: Eric Perdison, WFP Regional Director for Eastern and Southern Africa
a3958.speech: "A meal at school is more than just feeding a child. It is also an investment in the family, the community and, ultimately, the future of the country."

a3958.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3958.speech: Reaffirmed its commitment to continue supporting fragile contexts such as the Democratic Republic of Congo, Somalia and South Sudan, while calling for increased mobilisation of governments and international partners, noting that the lack of national financing and the decline in external aid are holding back lasting programmes.

a3984.speaker: José Maria Neves, President of the Republic of Cape Verde
a3984.speech: At the 36th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the African Union, warned about the specificities of the Small Island States that are part of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), asking for special attention for the smallest countries.

a3984.speaker: Services of the Presidency of the Republic (communiqué)
a3984.speech: Announced, through a communiqué, that for logistical and financial reasons the President of the Republic would not be present at the meeting of ECOWAS Heads of State and Government scheduled for 4 June.

a3984.speaker: Jorge Carlos Fonseca, President of the Republic of Cape Verde
a3984.speech: Said the ECOWAS Heads of State and Government decided today, at an extraordinary summit, that the transition period in Mali should not go beyond 12 months.

a3984.speaker: Source in the Guinean (Guinea-Bissau) Government (anonymous)
a3984.speech: Told Lusa that the chiefs of the Armed Forces of Senegal, Nigeria, Niger and Togo arrived in Bissau yesterday for a series of meetings with the political and military authorities of Guinea-Bissau.

a4116.speaker: The US-brokered Rwanda–Congo peace agreement (text of the agreement)
a4116.speech: Kinshasa and Kigali will also launch a regional economic integration framework within 90 days, the agreement said ; the agreement signed on Friday gives Congo and Rwanda three months to launch a framework "to expand foreign trade and investment derived from regional critical mineral supply chains" ; The agreement signed on Friday voiced "full support" for the Qatar-hosted talks ; It also says Congo and Rwanda will form a joint security coordination mechanism within 30 days and implement a plan agreed last year to monitor and verify the withdrawal of Rwandan soldiers within three months ; The agreement signed on Friday says Rwanda and Congo will de-risk mineral supply chains and establish value chains "that link both countries, in partnership, as appropriate, with the U.S. and U.S. investors."

a4116.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a4116.speech: "They were going at it for many years, and with machetes - it is one of the worst, one of the worst wars that anyone has ever seen. And I just happened to have somebody that was able to get it settled," Trump said on Friday, ahead of the signing of the deal in Washington ; "We're getting, for the United States, a lot of the mineral rights from the Congo as part of it. They're so honored to be here. They never thought they'd be coming." ; Trump warned of "very severe penalties, financial and otherwise", if the agreement is violated.

a4116.speaker: Olivier Nduhungirehe, Rwandan Foreign Minister
a4116.speech: called the agreement a turning point ; told Trump that past deals had not been implemented and urged Trump to stay engaged.

a4116.speaker: Therese Kayikwamba Wagner, Congo Foreign Minister
a4116.speech: said it must be followed by disengagement.

a4116.speaker: Massad Boulos, Trump's senior adviser for Africa
a4116.speech: dubbed the package of agreements the "Washington Accord" ; told Reuters in May that Washington wanted the peace agreement and accompanying minerals deals to be signed simultaneously this summer.

a4116.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a4116.speech: said on Friday that heads of state would be "here in Washington in a few weeks to finalize the complete protocol and agreement."

a4116.speaker: A source familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a4116.speech: told Reuters on Friday that another agreement on the framework would be signed by the heads of state at a separate White House event at an unspecified time ; There is an understanding that progress in ongoing talks in Doha - a separate but parallel mediation effort with delegations from the Congolese government and M23 - is essential before the signing of the economic framework, the source said.

a4116.speaker: Analysts and diplomats
a4116.speech: Rwanda has sent at least 7,000 soldiers over the border, according to analysts and diplomats, in support of the M23 rebels.

a4116.speaker: Reuters
a4116.speech: Reuters reported on Thursday that Congolese negotiators had dropped an earlier demand that Rwandan troops immediately leave eastern Congo, paving the way for the signing ceremony on Friday.

a4116.speaker: Congo, the United Nations and Western powers
a4116.speech: say Rwanda is supporting M23 by sending troops and arms.

a4116.speaker: Rwanda
a4116.speech: has long denied helping M23, saying its forces are acting in self-defence against Congo's army and ethnic Hutu militiamen linked to the 1994 Rwandan genocide, including the FDLR.

a4116.speaker: Jason Stearns, political scientist at Simon Fraser University in Canada
a4116.speech: "This is the best chance we have at a peace process for the moment despite all the challenges and flaws" ; Similar formulas have been attempted before, Stearns added, and "it will be up to the U.S., as they are the godfather of this deal, to make sure both sides abide by the terms."

a4116.speaker: Tresor Kibangula, political analyst at Congo's Ebuteli research institute
a4116.speech: The terms carry "a strategic message: securing the east also means securing investments" ; "It remains to be seen whether this economic logic will suffice" to end the fighting, he added.

a4125.speaker: Campbell (2004), cited study
a4125.speech: Cited as the source for the account that artisanal gold mining emerged in the 13th century in the Mali Empire, which extended as far as Agadez in Niger.

a4125.speaker: EITI 2021 report (Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative) / DGD 2021 customs data
a4125.speech: According to the EITI 2021 report, artisanal and small-scale mining gold exports in Niger reached 44.146 tonnes for a customs value of 370,620,409,394 FCFA, with the United Arab Emirates as the main destination — clearly lower than production and marketing data, demonstrating an inconsistency between the production, marketing and export of gold in Niger.

a4125.speaker: Field data (Niger gold-panning sites)
a4125.speech: According to field data, the lack of an effective management strategy and the porosity of Niger's borders are the main causes of the illegal flows of Nigerien artisanal gold.

a4125.speaker: USAID (2017), cited report
a4125.speech: Cited as the source for the figure that artisanal gold mining operations account for 15 to 20% of world gold production.

a4125.speaker: Oumar El Farouk et al. (2022), research study
a4125.speech: According to the results of their work, concentrations of trace metal elements in certain wells and boreholes at the gold-panning sites of the Nigerien Liptako are higher than WHO reference values and Nigerien standards — arsenic at 202.72 µg/l against a WHO standard of 10 µg/l, barium at 1,344.26 µg/l and manganese at 956 µg/l.

a4125.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) standards / Nigerien and French standards
a4125.speech: Cited as the reference values for drinking-water concentrations of arsenic (10 µg/l), barium (1,300 µg/l) and manganese (400 µg/l) against which the gold-panning site measurements were compared.

a4125.speaker: Several field actors
a4125.speech: Have made the link between gold panning, terrorism, banditry and illegal trafficking.

a4125.speaker: Gold-panning actors (field surveys, Nigerien Liptako)
a4125.speech: Expressed a real health concern about the appearance of dermatological and pulmonary diseases whose origin they do not know.

a4125.speaker: Dr Maman Illatou Oumar El Farouk, Nigerien researcher and developer of the LIPTAKOR tool (author of the article)
a4125.speech: States that his research work consisted in finding a solution making it possible to work with all gold-panning actors, bringing into synergy the knowledge derived from scientific research and the knowledge of gold panners, and that the serious game “LIPTAKOR” was developed to transfer the knowledge acquired during his doctoral work in order to strengthen actors' capacities on environmental and health issues and promote institutional reform of the sector (Cercau et al., 2024); argues it is necessary to roll out the game at other gold-panning sites in Niger and in other countries concerned by artisanal gold mining, and that if gold panning is well supervised it will improve the population's living conditions and the State's tax revenues.

a4125.speaker: Participants / gold-panning actors at the July 2021 Téra workshop
a4125.speech: At the end of the sessions, said they had acquired new knowledge about the regulatory frameworks that govern their activities and an understanding of practices harmful to the environment and to human and animal health; they expressed the need to formalise their activities.

a4125.speaker: Hassenforder et al. (2020), cited methodology
a4125.speech: Cited as the source of the observation grids on know-how, knowledge and perceptions used to evaluate the workshop results.

a4213.speaker: Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a4213.speech: “If Washington intends to destroy Russian-American relations, let that be on its conscience (…) The language of sanctions, whatever their scale, is useless with Russia.”

a4213.speaker: Petro Poroshenko, new Ukrainian President
a4213.speech: Said the hardening of tone by Washington and Brussels constitutes “an important step in support of Ukraine’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence.”

a4213.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a4213.speech: Reacted: “We are not seeking a temporary effect and do not wish to copy the methods of the American administration (…) We will not respond to the provocation and will act calmly,” after having spoken of an “impasse” with “serious damage” to Russian-American relations.

a4213.speaker: Sergei Ryabkov, Russian Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
a4213.speech: Had suggested that their response to this “scandalous” and “totally unacceptable” new wave of sanctions would be received in Washington in a “painful manner.”

a4215.speaker: Sunday Ogidigbo, Lead Pastor of Holyhill Church, Abuja (opinion article)
a4215.speech: Writes that “Nigeria stands today at a difficult but decisive crossroad” and that the country has lost decades to military rule, the oil boom to waste and corruption, countless lives to insecurity and poor healthcare, trust in institutions and many of its brightest minds ; argues that “Nigeria is now at that turning point. We must move from rhetoric to resolve, from promises to policy, from delays to decisive action,” that government must accelerate efforts to industrialise the economy, modernise agriculture and build mega-infrastructure ; contends that the resistance against the Dangote Refinery “is not just economic; it is symbolic,” representing a clash between the old order that thrived on import dependency and the new vision of industrial self-sufficiency, and that there are those whose fortunes depend on Nigeria remaining in perpetual blackout ; warns that “government cannot do it alone. The citizens must be ready to pay the price of transformation,” and concludes: “This is the turning point… We have lost a lot. But we must not lose the future. The next decade is our proving ground.”

a4441.speaker: Adewale Giwa, Senior Pastor of The Second Coming of Christ's Ministry
a4441.speech: Made the observation while addressing the congregation in Akure that Nigeria's socio-economic challenges require a leader who is ready to sacrifice him or herself ; He reminded his congregation about the prayer he asked them to say a fortnight ago that God should expose the troublers of Nigeria ; Asked rhetorically who was ready to sacrifice him or herself to save Nigeria: "Leader who wants to transform Nigeria will have to sacrifice himself. So, if a leader that truly wants to transform Nigeria, he has to sacrifice himself. So, who is ready?"

a4441.speaker: Adewale Giwa, Senior Pastor of The Second Coming of Christ's Ministry
a4441.speech: Noted that Nigerians should not expect the Western world to come and help them build their nation ; Emphasized that the Western world is not comfortable with any African leaders who are focused in placing their countries in good pedestal ; He referred to the late Libyan President, Muammar Gaddafi, accusing the West of being behind his killing, and recalled that Libyans were enjoying the nation until Gaddafi was murdered.

a4441.speaker: Adewale Giwa, Senior Pastor of The Second Coming of Christ's Ministry
a4441.speech: "You remember foreigners are the problems facing Nigeria. Just a few days ago, a publication came up from the United States of America, a lawmaker from the US Republican exposed a lot of things concerning the crisis going on in Africa. He exposed what the former US President Obama-led administration was doing with USAID in Nigeria. I am not surprised about this. I am not surprised at all. Obama campaigned for President Muhammadu Buhari during the election. They used Chibok Girls to discredit the administration of President Goodluck Jonathan."

a4441.speaker: Republican lawmaker in the United States (unnamed)
a4441.speech: A statement credited to a republican lawmaker accusing the President Barack Obama-led administration of contributing to the crisis in Nigeria, which the cleric alluded to.

a4446.speaker: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique H. Peter Vrooman
a4446.speech: "We are deeply concerned about the devastating impact of Cyclone Freddy on the people of Mozambique," said U.S. Ambassador H. Peter Vrooman. "This assistance will provide critical support to address the urgent needs of Mozambicans."

a4446.speaker: U.S. Government / USAID (press statement)
a4446.speech: Announced that the U.S. Government, through USAID, granted three humanitarian assistance awards totaling $5,750,000 to the World Food Program (WFP), International Organization for Migration (IOM), and United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) to provide urgent assistance to the victims of Cyclone Freddy in Mozambique, obligated $450,000 to Care International for shelter and WASH kits, and supports Save the Children and iDE for the second planting season, with total U.S. emergency assistance now exceeding $6 million ; Stated that the funding will provide 30 days of emergency food assistance to 135,000 people and shelter kits to over 7,500 households, along with extensive water and sanitation support, rapid rehabilitation of health facilities, cholera-containment WASH interventions, and mental health and protective support in hardest-hit Zambézia province ; Stated that the U.S. government is the leading international donor of humanitarian assistance in Mozambique, with humanitarian funding in 2022 alone totaling $176.7 million and more than $700 million in annual assistance provided in close collaboration with the Government of the Republic of Mozambique.

a4710.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4710.speech: Told the joint session of Congress: "We have accomplished more in 43 days than most administrations accomplished in four years or eight years, and we are just getting started." ; Said that "many" believed his to be the most successful start to a presidency in US history; noted what he said was a change in the national mood toward "pride" and "confidence"; compared himself to George Washington and boasted about the size of his electoral victory; ticked through a lengthy list of tangible accomplishments - hundreds of executive orders and actions, a freeze on foreign aid, lower levels of illegal border crossing, and the withdrawal from international organisations and agreements.

a4710.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4710.speech: Spoke at length about his ban on transgender athletes in women's sports and moves to get "woke ideology" out of US schools and the military: "Wokeness is trouble. Wokeness is bad. It's gone, it's gone, and we feel so much better for it, don't we?"

a4710.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4710.speech: Repeatedly blamed the Democrats, former President Joe Biden and "radical left lunatics" for all the nation's ills; needled his political adversaries, mocking their refusal to cheer his remarks, dusting off his "Pocahontas" nickname for Massachusetts Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren, and wryly noting that attempts to prosecute him "didn't work out" for his opponents.

a4710.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4710.speech: Said "small business optimism" was up but blamed Biden for the current state of the economy - including high egg prices; promised to "rescue" the economy and make getting "dramatic and immediate relief to working families" his highest priority.

a4710.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4710.speech: Called out Elon Musk in the audience and said his Department of Government Efficiency (Doge) would reduce inflation by cutting wasteful spending and fraud, prompting him to recite a laundry list of purported examples in foreign aid and other government programmes.

a4710.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4710.speech: Leaned heavily into promises of further progress on immigration enforcement and offered an animated defence of his tariff policies, saying that they were "protecting the soul of our country"; acknowledged that adding a tax on imported goods from Canada, Mexico and China might cause a "disturbance" and that US farmers might feel a "period of indigestion"; promised to move forward with reciprocal tariffs on all US trade partners next month.

a4710.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4710.speech: Once again promised to balance the budget, providing no details about the kind of steep cuts such a promise would require, and turned to discussing the tax cuts he hopes Congress will enact - including his campaign promises of no taxes on tips, overtime or Social Security.

a4710.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4710.speech: Repeated his desire for an American annexation of Greenland, promised American control of the Panama Canal and only made brief mention of Gaza and the Middle East; spoke more extensively about negotiating with Russia for peace in Ukraine; after reading Zelensky's letter, said "I appreciate that", offering a hint of a possible cooling of the acrimony between the two leaders, and added that Zelensky had said he was ready to sign an agreement on minerals and security "at any time that is convenient for you".

a4710.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine (in a letter read out by Trump, similar to a message posted on X)
a4710.speech: "My team and I stand ready to work under President Trump's strong leadership to get a peace that lasts. We do really value how much America has done to help Ukraine maintain its sovereignty and independence."

a4710.speaker: Al Green, Texas Democratic Congressman
a4710.speech: Harangued the president at the very start of Trump's speech, his mostly inaudible comments punctuated with repeated thrusts of his cane; would tell reporters outside the Capitol that he was protesting proposed cuts to the government-run Medicaid health insurance for low-income Americans.

a4710.speaker: Mike Johnson, Speaker of the House
a4710.speech: Called for decorum, after which the House Sergeant-at-Arms escorted the congressman from the chamber.

a4710.speaker: Democratic legislators (several dozen)
a4710.speech: Responded by holding up small black signs with words like "false" and "lies".

a4710.speaker: Most economists
a4710.speech: Warn that Trump's tariffs will lead to higher prices for American consumers.

a4886.speaker: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (Unctad) (analysis)
a4886.speech: observed that with only two percent of the potential was being utilised, a carbon price of $100 per tonne is needed, without which approximately 97 percent of their mitigation potential could go untapped by 2050 ; “The market value of carbon credits does not represent the actual size of financial transfers to the LDC host countries of underlying projects, since significant shares of the value created by the mitigation activities are taken by brokers, resellers and other intermediaries operating in those markets. Carbon projects currently provide only a minor contribution towards meeting the enormous investment needs of LDCs’ energy sectors.” ; said in 2023, the estimated market value of LDC-sourced carbon credits was $403 million, corresponding to about one percent of net bilateral official development assistance flows from traditional donors ; has since urged LDCs and their partners to strengthen domestic regulations, enhance international cooperation and build to unlock economic opportunities through carbon markets while advancing global climate goals.

a4886.speaker: Unctad (limiting effect of untapped potential)
a4886.speech: According to Unctad, this untapped potential has limited the economies’ financial returns, which are modest compared to larger sources of funding like development aid, foreign direct investment, and remittances.

a4886.speaker: Ministry of Natural Resources and Climate Change of Malawi (data/statement)
a4886.speech: Data from the Ministry shows that Malawi has earned K150 million from the sale of about 75 000 carbon credits through projects under the Green Development Mechanism and Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (Redd+) programme ; the Ministry said the carbon credit initiative in Malawi has the potential to generate $600 million (about K1.05 trillion) annually.

a4886.speaker: Werani Chilenga, Parliamentary Committee on Natural Resources and Climate Change chairperson
a4886.speech: is on record as having said lack of a legal framework to regulate and sanitise the industry has left the sector less attractive to serious players. “As we speak, we don’t have the Carbon Credit Act to regulate the sector and if we have any policy I have not seen it.”

a4886.speaker: Rebeca Grynspan, Unctad secretary general
a4886.speech: noted in an accompanying statement that while carbon markets are seen as catalysts of capital flows towards developing countries, they are not a panacea that can solve the pressing issue of financing sustainable development in the LDCs. “They are not a substitute for official development assistance or for climate finance flows, particularly for adaptation, which is these countries’ priority.”

a4886.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a4886.speech: listed carbon credits as one of Malawi’s potential game changers, a pathway for the country to generate the much-needed foreign exchange and restore Malawi’s degraded forests.

a5019.speaker: Jacob Warchum (Warchum Duke), Information Minister of the Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a5019.speech: Says nearly 160 households have so far been displaced by severe flooding in Pochalla South and Pochalla North counties; told Eye Radio that the flooding began when the Kovu River burst its banks in Pochalla South and has now spread to Pochalla North, where the Oboth River has also overflowed, damaging crops, cutting off roads, and displacing more communities; warned that the situation is worsening, with hundreds now in urgent need of shelter and assistance; said many of the displaced are now sheltering in schools and public buildings, while others remain in the open without protection: “About 158 households are currently being accommodated in the schools and other available facilities within Pecheneg South headquarters. So, the local authorities are assessing the damage and advising the affected families to seek a temporary shelter in nearby towns, including the county school facilities and apartments” ; “So, this is the current situation where Pochalla South residents are. Right. So, what is the condition of those displaced? They are in a very bad situation because they are sleeping in an open area. There is no shelter, and most of them are with children, the women.”

a5019.speaker: Jacob Warchum (Warchum Duke), Information Minister of the Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a5019.speech: Said malaria cases have already been reported, and they’re appealing for immediate humanitarian assistance: “So up to now, there’s no immediate intervention yet done in those two locations. It is dire because, you know, when there is flooding like this, we are expecting some diseases like malaria. And then dry forth because the water will be very dirty. People will be on fire in one place. So there is a high risk of waterborne diseases that may also arise from there. So people are in fear of that.
