So there is already an issue of malaria cases being reported there also.”

a5148.speaker: Nouhoum Sarr, member of the National Transition Council (CNT) and president of the African Front for Development (FAD) party
a5148.speech: gave his verdict on the record of the Transition, which in his eyes is eloquent: “With all due respect to the little sorcerers whose agenda is clear: to bring down the saviours of Mali…” ; reacting on his Facebook wall: “The record speaks, the figures are eloquent, let us never lose sight of them. It is a constant in politics that when you are fought against, nothing is fair. You will take blows; forgetting to give them back is suicidal. The record of the transition is eloquent, with all due respect to the little sorcerers whose agenda is clear, to bring down the saviours of Mali, they will not miss any opportunity to sap morale, fortunately the Malian people are still standing, the Prime Minister’s visit to Segou is verifiable proof of it.”

a5148.speaker: Nouhoum Sarr, member of the National Transition Council (CNT) and president of the African Front for Development (FAD) party
a5148.speech: added that in less than five years the Malian Army has gone from 22,000 to more than 65,000 men with individual weapons; that recruitment of judicial auditors went from 316 to between 400 and 716 to strengthen the Magistracy; and that more than 2,000 new civil servants were recruited. “The largest armament programme the country has ever known from Sundiata to our day. The return of more than 90,000 km2 to the national fold (Kidal, Ber, Tessalit etc…). All of this with the national budget, without any foreign aid. They were never able to do it when they were in power,” hammered Mr Sarr. He also mentioned that they are ready on every front to preserve the gains and defend their record, which is not comparable to the 30 years of past management.

a5148.speaker: Internet users (commenters on the Facebook post)
a5148.speech: after this post, many internet users hit back and dismissed Mr Sarr’s reaction as a “failed outing”.

a5151.speaker: “Philosoph”, Rwandan refugee at Tongogara Refugee Settlement (nickname used at his request)
a5151.speech: asked that just his nickname be used because he fears retribution; recounted that after nearly two decades at the settlement he, his wife and 10 others were set to leave for resettlement in the United States on January 21, and that one day before he received the heartbreaking news that, due to an executive order by US President Donald Trump, their resettlement was cancelled.

a5151.speaker: US State Department
a5151.speech: In response to a request for comment, confirmed that it has “suspended refugee arrivals and case processing activities.” It did not provide any other details.

a5151.speaker: Johanne Mhlanga, settlement administrator at Tongogara Refugee Settlement
a5151.speech: says more than 1,300 refugees from the settlement were resettled in the US in 2024 and 887 new submissions were made that year.

a5151.speaker: 2024 Refugee Council US report
a5151.speech: According to a 2024 Refugee Council US report, in 2024 over 100,000 refugees were resettled in the US through the US Refugee Admissions Programme — the highest number admitted in one year since 1994.

a5163.speaker: Israeli local press
a5163.speech: Reported that Israel’s security cabinet approved during the night of Sunday a plan to resume humanitarian aid access in Gaza, which has been completely blocked since 2 March.

a5163.speaker: Israel Hayom (Israeli daily)
a5163.speech: According to the daily, the cabinet also approved a gradual increase of military pressure on the enclave and pressuring Hamas to accept a ceasefire.

a5163.speaker: Yediot Ahronot (Israeli daily)
a5163.speech: Reports that some ministers opposed the idea of allowing food, medicine and other essential goods to be distributed again in the Palestinian territory, after a blockade of more than two months.

a5163.speaker: Itamar Ben Gvir, Israeli Minister of National Security
a5163.speech: Said during the meeting that “there is no need to bring aid into Gaza” and that “Hamas’s food warehouses should be bombed,” provoking what the local press described as a heated argument with the Army Chief of Staff, Eyal Zamir.

a5197.speaker: Ambassador Dorothy Shea, US charge d'affaires ad interim to the United Nations
a5197.speech: At a UN Security Council briefing on the Democratic Republic of the Congo on 28 January 2024 in New York, explained that the United States condemns the capture of Goma and urges the Council to consider measures to put an end to the territorial advances of Rwandan troops and the M23 ; indicated that the United States firmly supports the Congolese people, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, and urges Rwanda to respect them ; “We call for an immediate ceasefire and an end to this fighting. Rwanda must withdraw its troops from the DRC” ; said Rwanda and the DRC must return to the negotiating table and work toward a lasting and peaceful solution.

a5197.speaker: Ambassador Dorothy Shea, US charge d'affaires ad interim to the United Nations
a5197.speech: Stated that the United States is watching with concern and deplores the destruction of diplomatic facilities in Kinshasa, and calls on the government of the DRC to respect its obligations to protect diplomatic premises and personnel.

a5197.speaker: Ambassador Dorothy Shea, US charge d'affaires ad interim to the United Nations
a5197.speech: Said she is deeply concerned about the human rights violations, the displacement and the other consequences for Congolese civilians who suffer most from this fighting, and that civilians, in particular the growing number of internally displaced persons and refugees in Sake, Goma and beyond, must be protected ; said that more than ever humanitarian actors must be allowed to operate freely and to deliver life-saving aid, and that the rights of all the inhabitants of Goma, including former combatants, must be respected ; said she is concerned that the continued advances of the M23 and Rwanda are opening a new bloody front in this conflict in South Kivu, which no longer benefits from the roles assumed by MONUSCO in the past to protect civilians and facilitate humanitarian aid ; “We must not allow this violence to degenerate into a broader regional conflict, which would entail a terrible human toll” ; added that UN and humanitarian organisation personnel, as well as civilians, are being put at risk by Rwanda's continued use of GPS interference and its deployment of sophisticated weapons and systems.

a5197.speaker: Ambassador Dorothy Shea, US charge d'affaires ad interim to the United Nations
a5197.speech: Said the United States mourns all the Congolese who have lost their lives in this fighting and extends its most sincere condolences to the countries and the families of the UN peacekeepers and the SAMIDRC soldiers killed in these attacks ; praised MONUSCO for its commitment to protecting civilians and for the courage and professionalism shown by the peacekeepers in recent weeks.

a5197.speaker: Ambassador Dorothy Shea, US charge d'affaires ad interim to the United Nations
a5197.speech: Said she remains convinced that hope is not lost, that an end to the fighting and a path toward regional dialogue are in sight, but the international community must act now, and that those who do not wish to return to the negotiating table must face a clear and unambiguous response from the Council ; “We must abandon the illusion of short-term military solutions and instead work toward a lasting peace fuelled by regional economic agreements on the vast mineral wealth of the Great Lakes, in order to guarantee stability and prosperity for local populations. The resolution of historical grievances, the end of ethnic attacks and of the other causes of this conflict must come about through a process that includes clear incentives and unambiguous accountability. The international community has the tools in hand to end the fighting and find lasting solutions to the conflict in eastern DRC.”

a5211.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President, and Sir Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister
a5211.speech: Have said France and the UK will support Ukraine for as long as necessary “to thwart Russia's war of aggression”.

a5211.speaker: Elysee Palace (statement)
a5211.speech: Said the two leaders had reaffirmed their commitment to “support Ukraine unwaveringly” ; said the two leaders had reaffirmed their commitment to “support Ukraine unwaveringly and for as long as necessary to thwart Russia's war of aggression”.

a5211.speaker: Downing Street (statement)
a5211.speech: Said the pair discussed how to put Ukraine in “the strongest possible position going into the winter”.

a5211.speaker: Downing Street
a5211.speech: Said “no war was ever won by a single weapon” when asked whether the UK was speaking to President Biden about the potential use of the missiles.

a5211.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a5211.speech: Said he could end the war “in one day”.

a5321.speaker: USAID termination note of March 3 2025 (document)
a5321.speech: Cited as the source showing that HIV and Aids, maternal health, education, governance and economic development funding have all been erased, with health the most affected area — HIV and Aids in Malawi alone losing $163 521 653 (about K283.5 billion); affected projects include Empower, Protect, Core, Prevention (Kuteteza), Ana ndi Achinyamata Patsogolo and the Momentum components; education losses of $2.82 million for Tisamale Mabuku and $1 057 846 for Transforming Higher Education Systems; $2.64 million for the Economic Growth Policy project; $1 531 114 for the Strengthening Electoral Integrity Project; and a combined $13.5 million for two governance projects.

a5321.speaker: US State Department
a5321.speech: According to the US State Department, USAid was forking $350 million (K630 billion) to Malawi yearly.

a5321.speaker: Development economist with expertise in analysing foreign aid (anonymous)
a5321.speech: Said in an interview that the withdrawal of aid through USAid was only a tip of the iceberg and that Malawi should expect reduction of aid through all United Nations agencies where the USA has also cut funding ; “Aid is a product of progress that those countries do, and the business environment is messed up, so countries like the United Kingdom [UK] and even the European Union will reduce aid because their fiscal space has reduced due to bottlenecks that the USA has put.” ; “Malawi needs to develop very strong relations with China, India and Russia, convince them to give us aid. For countries like India, they may attach that to business and we have to go for it. Let us look to the East.”

a5321.speaker: United Kingdom (government announcement)
a5321.speech: Announced that it would cut its foreign aid to 0.3 percent of gross national product from 0.5 percent to free up money for defence spending amid growing threats from Russia and collapsing security guarantees from the USA.

a5321.speaker: Thomas Chataghalala Munthali, National Planning Commission director general
a5321.speech: Said they have commissioned a study into what the withdrawal of USA aid will mean for Malawi.

a5321.speaker: Gowokani Chijere-Chirwa, economist
a5321.speech: Said Malawi has to look into other financing models for health ; “For example, the housing and construction sector all are not taxed. Not only that, the lack of digitisation in business makes Malawi fail to collect required revenue since we are not sure who is making how much money.” ; “In other countries, they have a compulsory health surcharge for people coming in the country from other countries and it does not matter whether you will go to public or private facility, can we also try that?”

a5321.speaker: Khumbidze Kandodo Chiponda, Health Minister
a5321.speech: Did not respond to our queries yesterday; said during the Boma Likutinji media briefing that Malawi still has HIV and Aids, Malaria and TB commodities until 2026 from the Global Fund.

a5321.speaker: Williams Banda, Ministry of Finance spokesperson
a5321.speech: Said only K9.2 billion of USAid funding appears in the 2024/25 National Budget.

a5321.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5321.speech: In January issued an executive order for a 90-day halt in foreign assistance pending a review of efficiencies and consistency with his foreign policy.

a5331.speaker: Donald Trump, US presidential candidate
a5331.speech: Said certain words demeaning to the female gender when he competed against Hillary Clinton, the first time a woman ran for the presidency in America.

a5580.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso, chaired by President of Faso Captain Ibrahim Traoré (official record)
a5580.speech: Judged the execution of the State budget for financial year 2024 satisfactory, reflecting great rigour, good efficiency and an ability to adapt in the face of the challenges encountered, and gave its agreement for the transmission of the draft budget settlement act to the Transitional Legislative Assembly.

a5580.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (official record)
a5580.speech: Adopted a draft decree revising decree no. 2025-0643/PRES/PM/MEF of 28 May 2025 on transit activities for dangerous or strategic materials, stating that the revision is required in order to extend the competence of the State company Faso Transit et Logistique to goods benefiting from exemption from import or export duties and taxes, and aims to strengthen State control over these sensitive flows, which are liable to constitute vectors for uncontrolled transactions and to undermine national security as well as public finances.

a5580.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (official record)
a5580.speech: Adopted a draft decree setting the list of products subject to Special Import Authorisation (ASI) and Special Export Authorisation (ASE), stating that the revision aims to take into account other products and to comply with the new law on plastic packaging and bags, and will support the Government’s policy of autonomous and structuring financing for the development of the agricultural, pastoral and fishery sectors — adding three new products on import and eight on export.

a5580.speaker: Government / Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso (official record)
a5580.speech: Stated that in view of the non-responsiveness of the 37 shareholders holding the remaining 305 shares (0.0375% of capital), the Government decided to proceed with the expropriation of the minority shareholders concerned, the decree enshrining the full takeover of SN SOSUCO by the State of Burkina Faso.

a5580.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad
a5580.speech: Communication to the Council on the visit of a 1,200-strong delegation of people of African descent from the African Diaspora Development Institute (ADDI), scheduled from 26 October to 8 November 2025, whose aims include strengthening the historical and cultural ties between Africa and its diasporas, exploring economic opportunities in strategic sectors with prospects for direct investment, and bringing ADDI’s support to the President of Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, who is a symbol of dignity and resistance in Africa and within the diaspora.

a5580.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad
a5580.speech: Communication reporting on Burkina Faso’s participation in the 3rd United Nations Conference on Landlocked Developing Countries, held from 5 to 8 August 2025 in Awaza, Turkmenistan, where the delegation reported on the country’s achievements in rehabilitating the road network, extending national electricity coverage and strengthening telecommunications infrastructure thanks to increased mobilisation of domestic resources and bold tax and customs reforms; said the Conference was also an opportunity for the member states of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) to speak with one voice, a common position carried by the Prime Minister of Mali attesting to a progressive recognition of the Confederation by international bodies.

a5580.speaker: Minister of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity
a5580.speech: Communication on the commemoration of the 28th edition of the International Day of Rural Women, scheduled for 15 October 2025 in the rural commune of Barsalogho, Koulse region, under the theme “Agro-pastoral and fisheries offensive in Burkina Faso: what strategies for a better contribution of rural women in the localities of return?”, aimed at strengthening the productive capacities of returned rural women and supporting their socio-economic reintegration.

a5580.speaker: Minister of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity
a5580.speech: Communication taking stock of the 17th edition of Solidarity Month, held from 4 November to 3 December 2024 under the theme “Solidarity, a factor of social cohesion”: as at 5 May 2025 the total resources mobilised amount to 272,225,110 CFA francs, of which 194,691,500 CFA francs in financial contributions — to strengthen health care for indigent patients including internally displaced persons and support the social and economic empowerment of women — and 77,533,610 CFA francs in kind, immediately made available to vulnerable people in the various regions.

a5580.speaker: Minister of Health
a5580.speech: Communication on the results of the third round (P2) of the Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention Plus (CPS+) campaign for 2025, held from 21 to 24 August 2025 across all 70 health districts: of an expected target of 4,825,891 children aged 3 to 59 months, 4,785,318 were treated, an administrative coverage rate of 99.16%; 97.76% were treated door to door; 36,344 moderately acutely malnourished children and 12,126 severely acutely malnourished children were screened or caught up; the districts of Sebba, Tougouri and Pama experienced a delay in the supply of inputs, and the next round takes place from 18 to 21 September 2025 in 67 districts.

a5580.speaker: Minister of Higher Education, Research and Innovation
a5580.speech: Reported to the Council on the mission of a delegation from the Biodiversity Information Centre (InfoBio) of Joseph KI-ZERBO University, from 15 to 20 August 2025 in Lomé, Togo, which made it possible to define a strategy for pooling research infrastructure and teams with a view to establishing centres of excellence, and said a draft framework agreement will be initiated and discussed for cooperation between the University of Lomé and Joseph KI-ZERBO University.

a5680.speaker: Isálcio Mahanjane, lawyer for António Carlos do Rosário and Bruno Langa (also represents Ndambi Guebuza)
a5680.speech: Told Lusa on Friday that three more people convicted in the hidden debt scandal had been released, including Gregório Leão, former director-general of the Mozambican secret service ; “Their preventive detention has been lifted under the parole regime.”

a5680.speaker: The court in the hidden debts case
a5680.speech: Ruled, according to the court, that Fabião Mabunda was a construction technician who owned a company that received bribes from Privinvest ; found it proven that the defendants were bribed to facilitate meetings with the former Mozambican president and influence the approval of the coastal protection project used to raise the money that fuelled the hidden debts involving the Privinvest shipyards ; ruled that assets it considered to be “proceeds of crime” by the convicted defendants should be forfeited to the state.

a5680.speaker: Efigénio Baptista, judge in the hidden debts case
a5680.speech: Sentenced six of the 19 official suspects to 12 years in prison, the highest sentence handed down on the last day of the reading of the sentence in Maputo.

a5680.speaker: Mozambican public prosecutor
a5680.speech: Presented figures according to which the debts, discovered in 2016, were estimated at around US$2.7 billion (more than €2.3 billion).

a5680.speaker: World Bank
a5680.speech: According to the World Bank, Mozambique was then one of the world's ten fastest-growing economies for two decades, but ended up plunging into financial turmoil after the case.

a5689.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President-elect of Malawi
a5689.speech: Threatened to deal with civil servants involved in dubious corrupt practices in the country, stating that the vice is retrogressive to the nation: “I have my eyes everywhere, and I know that a lot of things are going on in the government by civil servants. Huge payments are being made, money is being transferred, and dubious contracts are being honored. People doing this, including the politicians facilitating it, must stop because it is illegal and criminal.”

a5689.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President-elect of Malawi
a5689.speech: Called upon the public, regardless of political and cultural background, to work together with his administration to ensure that national transformation takes centre stage: “The challenges before us are real. I believe that with concerted efforts, unity, discipline, and hard work, we can rise above these challenges. We need to work together to ensure that the economy is recovered, food is available, jobs are created, infrastructure is improved, health and education systems are strengthened, and above all, public trust is built.”

a5689.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President-elect of Malawi
a5689.speech: Added that his administration is in the transitional process, and in the days to come he will unveil recovery and development plans for Malawi: “Our new administration will reflect our commitment to prudence, inclusion, competence, and delivery. Let us begin this new chapter with hope and humility, and with renewed purpose.”

a5689.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President-elect of Malawi
a5689.speech: Commended Malawians for giving him the mandate to govern the country again in the next five years: “This is not a victory for any individual or a party; it is a victory for our democracy, for our constitution, and most importantly, for every Malawian who believes in a better tomorrow.” ; also hailed outgoing President Lazarus Chakwera for conceding defeat, which he said demonstrated statesmanship.

a5689.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
a5689.speech: Declared Mutharika as President-elect along with Justice Jane Mayemu Ansah as Vice-President-elect following the September 16 presidential election, where he garnered 56.8% of the votes against his contender Chakwera, who secured 33%.

a5846.speaker: David Fode Faye, law lecturer at Assane Seck University of Ziguinchor (Senegal) and Managing Partner of Teranga LeX
a5846.speech: Said the term "legaltech" stands for "Legal Technology" and is "a neologism designating the use of technology to deliver legal services that are more efficient, accessible and affordable," including case management software, contract-processing platforms, automation of legal tasks, regulatory compliance solutions and predictive analytics tools ; noted that legaltechs appeared in the United States with RocketLawyer and Legalzoom around 2000 ; argued the notion is undergoing "a semantic diversion" because it now also designates the company or firm implementing the technology, so that "the content is taken for the container."

a5846.speaker: David Fode Faye, law lecturer at Assane Seck University of Ziguinchor (Senegal) and Managing Partner of Teranga LeX
a5846.speech: Said legaltech is "on the one hand, a response to the systemic problems of access to justice and to the law, and on the other hand, an alternative for better legal and judicial security" ; said introducing technology into law gives litigants and citizens much simpler access to information, noting that lawyers "often have a bad press, because the jargon is esoteric and generally reserved for insiders" ; noted a strong trend of digitalisation driven by state authorities in many African countries, including in the justice sector, and said the continent's economic potential and foreign direct investment push legal actors to align their practice with international standards, adding that Benin and the OHADA member states place great emphasis on legal and judicial security.

a5846.speaker: David Fode Faye, law lecturer at Assane Seck University of Ziguinchor (Senegal) and Managing Partner of Teranga LeX
a5846.speech: Said the assessment of the major developments in digital law and legaltech is "generally positive, with a few nuances to consider": legaltech "has made legal services more accessible to a broader range of people, in particular to those who cannot afford the high fees of traditional law firms," automation has let professionals focus on more strategic work and reduced costs for clients, case and contract management software has improved firms' operational efficiency, predictive analytics tools help assess legal risks and forecast dispute outcomes, and compliance solutions help companies meet regulations.

a5846.speaker: David Fode Faye, law lecturer at Assane Seck University of Ziguinchor (Senegal) and Managing Partner of Teranga LeX
a5846.speech: Said legaltech offers several potential solutions for improving access to justice in African jurisdictions: online platforms providing basic legal information (citing Senegal's "Journal fac droit"), online legal advisory services by chat or video call for those who cannot reach a law firm for geographical or financial reasons, and online mediation platforms for resolving small disputes without going to court (citing "JustiCity" and the "Mediation Academy South Africa"); said that by investing in such solutions governments, NGOs and companies can help overcome obstacles to access to justice.

a5846.speaker: David Fode Faye, law lecturer at Assane Seck University of Ziguinchor (Senegal) and Managing Partner of Teranga LeX
a5846.speech: Said the "apero du droit numerique" his organisation holds is a perfect example of promoting digital technologies, and noted that Tunisia, Senegal, Mali and Cote d'Ivoire have created legal frameworks to promote start-ups while Benin is preparing a draft decree granting tax advantages to "Innovative Young Digital Enterprises" (Jeni) ; said political will is needed and commended the efforts of the authorities, "who have understood that digital technology offers fine opportunities for development" ; endorsed the recommendations of the report on the state of Benin's digital ecosystem, urging multidimensional support to digital enterprises, a national digital skills framework, stronger public-private collaboration and access of small local digital firms to public procurement, a more inclusive evidence-based ecosystem, and the integration of digital training modules, the modernisation of justice and the democratisation of legal-sector skills.

a5846.speaker: Report "Status of the digital ecosystem and digital entrepreneurship in Benin"
a5846.speech: Cited as the source of the recommendations Faye endorses on supporting digital enterprises, developing digital skills, strengthening public-private collaboration and building a more inclusive, evidence-based digital ecosystem.

a5846.speaker: Draft decree of Benin on "Innovative Young Digital Enterprises" (Jeni)
a5846.speech: Cited (article 8) as providing that "any eligible and approved company benefits from the following tax advantages for the duration of enjoyment of the status: suspension of the business licence tax, suspension of value added tax, suspension of tax on profits, suspension of taxes relating to salaries and of the employer's payroll levy, suspension of registration and stamp duties at their creation."

a5893.speaker: Livelihood-Focused Climate Risk Assessment: Stress Testing Livelihood Options in the World’s Largest Terrestrial Transboundary Conservation Area Report (report by KAZA under USAID)
a5893.speech: Notes that shorter and increasingly variable rainfall patterns will decrease the reliability of rainfed agriculture, which is vital for regional food security ; “Drying patterns will constrain the growth of the tourism industry, as it relies heavily on water to support the wildlife that draws thousands of tourists every year.” ; notes that a longer dry season will also affect livestock production and compound more negative human-wildlife conflicts, requiring a more concerted effort to conserve and manage water to meet agricultural, wildlife and ecological demands.

a5893.speaker: Livelihood-Focused Climate Risk Assessment Report (KAZA/USAID)
a5893.speech: Notes that weather conditions are growing more perilous, increasing the likelihood of large, runaway fires following rainy seasons and threatening the viability of conservation and carbon storage opportunities and programmes ; “Our modeling also suggests that the spatial extent of flooding will increase and extend well beyond existing floodplains during future flood events.” ; notes that standing in harm’s way is an intricate network of roadways, tourist lodges and a patchwork of rural and urban unplanned settlements.

a5893.speaker: Livelihood-Focused Climate Risk Assessment Report (KAZA/USAID)
a5893.speech: Notes that solutions for adaptation exist and many resource- and climate-dependent livelihoods may endure in areas with adequate support; that activities such as farming, fishing and foraging can benefit from climate information services and expanded access to climate risk finance options; and that authorities can help incentivise personal adaptation by making financing more accessible, promoting indigenous knowledge and practices, delivering technical guidance, and ensuring necessary climate-adaptive materials are available in local markets.

a5893.speaker: Livelihood-Focused Climate Risk Assessment Report (KAZA/USAID)
a5893.speech: “Climate change is expected to increase average annual temperatures and the intensity, duration and frequency of extreme heat events, which will inevitably put a greater number of people at risk of heat-related medical conditions.” ; notes it will limit livestock and crop production, the time allocated to outdoor and physically demanding activities, and potentially affect the tourism season, due to a higher number of days exceeding known thresholds of thermal comfort levels ; “By mid-century, maximum temperatures during the hottest part of the year (October and November) over southern Africa are expected to increase by 2.5 to 3.5 degrees Celsius, and within KAZA, this assessment finds that very hot days (days above 35 degrees Celsius) could increase by two to threefold.”

a6041.speaker: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Vice President of Ghana
a6041.speech: Has said the perception that foreign aid to Africa was a one-sided act of charity was not true and that wealth flows out of the continent far more than it receives ; “You see, one of the questions he hasn't asked himself is how much leaves our continent for his [Donald Trump's] country. They think it's just charity. It is not” ; “If even a fraction of what is taken from our continent remained, we wouldn't have issues with unemployment, sanitation, or many other challenges” ; warned that Africa would not continue to accept economic imbalances: “At the right time, we'll also take action. And it will not be funny” ; referenced Niger's recent decision to renegotiate its mineral contracts, which saw its national revenue rise from $1 billion to over $10 billion in a year.

a6041.speaker: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Vice President of Ghana
a6041.speech: On climate justice, pointed out the unfair burden placed on African nations despite their minimal contributions to global emissions: “We are responsible for less than 5% [of emissions], yet we are expected to bear the consequences.”

a6041.speaker: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Vice President of Ghana
a6041.speech: Encouraged the students to amplify African perspectives in global conversations: “We need everybody's voice. You are from Harvard Kennedy School and MIT, we need your voices too.”

a6301.speaker: Mohamud Maallim Abdulle, Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SODMA), and Abdinasir Abdi Aroush, Minister of Relief of the Southern Administration
a6301.speech: Convened to advocate for public safety; they urged residents to avoid areas near waterways that are prone to flooding during this season.

a6403.speaker: Scott Perry, United States congressman
a6403.speech: Claimed during the inaugural session of the Congress' Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency (DOGE) that USAID funded Boko Haram and other terror groups, saying the agency's annual budget of $697 million, including cash shipments to madrasas, has inadvertently funded terrorist training camps and extremist groups: "Your money, $697 million annually, plus shipments of cash, funds ISIS, al-Qaeda, Boko Haram, ISIS Khorasan, and terrorist training camps" ; "That's what it's funding." He provided no evidence of his claim in the video.

a6403.speaker: Scott Perry, United States congressman
a6403.speech: Also faulted USAID's $136 million expenditure on building 120 schools in Pakistan, alleging that the schools were never constructed.

a6403.speaker: Many Democrats
a6403.speech: Saying Republicans are willing to demonise the US aid agency to kill it.

a6403.speaker: Richard Mills Jr, US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6403.speech: Disputed Mr Perry's allegation for lack of evidence, saying there was no evidence for it.

a6403.speaker: Senators Ali Ndume, Abdul Ningi and Kaka Shehu (Nigerian Senate)
a6403.speech: During a plenary session in February told the Senate to invite the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu; the Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency, Mohammed Mohammed; and the Director General of the State Security Services, Oluwatosin Ajayi, over Mr Perry's claims.

a6403.speaker: Godswill Akpabio, Senate President of Nigeria
a6403.speech: Granting their request, said the security helmsmen will appear before the lawmakers in a closed-door session to speak on Mr Perry's allegations against USAID.

a6403.speaker: US embassy in Nigeria (post on X)
a6403.speech: Posted a cryptic message on X saying it probed all assistance given to Nigeria to ensure it reached the intended recipients; it, however, condemned the "blatant disregard for human life perpetrated by Boko Haram."

a6403.speaker: Emmanuel Ogebe, US-based Nigerian human rights lawyer
a6403.speech: In a letter advised Mr Perry to either substantiate his claim or quickly repudiate it "regarding Boko Haram before anyone gets hurt"; "No political propaganda or showboating is worth putting Americans' lives at risk abroad for a lie," noting that Perry's "baseless" claims have "sent shockwaves through Nigeria and elicited targeting of innocent Christians and aid workers" ; "To make matters worse, you have further endangered hundreds of American diplomats in one of the largest U.S. embassies in the world, many of whom already lost their jobs due to the vampiric shutdown by lawless non-state actors in DC" ; recalled how a bomb attack on the US embassy compound in Abuja led to the displacement of American diplomats and their families: "They and their families were internationally displaced for months before returning in early 2023 to Nigeria" ; "For you to make such false and unfounded allegations, right after Musk's admission that USAID's $50 million condoms used for bombings by Hamas terrorists was untrue, irresponsibly jeopardises the security of American diplomats and their families, local Christians and aid workers in Nigeria." He also said he petitioned the US Department of Justice to investigate Mr Perry.

a6403.speaker: Scott Perry, United States congressman
a6403.speech: In his response dated 26 March avoided commenting about his previous allegation that USAID funded Boko Haram and instead focussed on irregularities such as waste, fraud and abuse by agencies like USAID which "have run rampant in the federal government for decades": "The main mission of DOGE is to ensure that the resources of hardworking American People are not squandered" ; "DOGE is going line-by-line across the federal budget inspecting and trying to eliminate waste - something for which I've fought and advocated since coming to Congress, so it has my full and enthusiastic support." He said USAID funded "partisan" media outlets like Politico, "which received over $8M (and almost $500K for 37 Politico Pro subscriptions at the FDA)", accused USAID of giving the Taliban $15 million for condoms, claimed the agency gave more than $446,000 to promote atheism in Nepal, $14 million in cash vouchers for non-citizens at the US southern border, $1.5 million for promoting jobs for LGBTQ persons in Serbia, $2.5 million for electric vehicle charging stations in Vietnam, over $425,000 to Indonesian coffee companies to help them become more climate and gender-friendly, more than $3.3 million in the Caribbean for "being LGBTQ", and $20 million for a Sesame Street-style show in Iraq: "This is all just the tip of the iceberg of USAID offenses; it's insanity - at best - and not only can USAID's end not come soon enough, but it must be investigated thoroughly for fraud and abuse of Taxpayer dollars" ; claimed that that was "too hard for many Members of Congress, the Executive branch, and bureaucrats to handle, let alone actually address" ; "So now that DOGE was allowed to deep-dive into the stunning grift of USAID, it certainly has my full support here as well."

a6403.speaker: Scott Perry, United States congressman
a6403.speech: Spoke on how DOGE is tampering with personal information, exonerating the body of such misconduct: "DOGE has no access to the Treasury's tax and Social Security data" ; "As a Member on the House Oversight Committee, I will continue to ensure the safety and security of Americans' personal data."

a6403.speaker: Scott Perry, United States congressman
a6403.speech: Applauded President Trump's executive action but noted that the government's efficiency needs to be codified: "I have introduced a Balanced Budget Amendment to the Constitution every Session that I've been in Congress. It requires the federal government to balance its budget and limit it to spending only what it takes in each year" ; "President Trump has taken the first step towards fiscal sanity, now it's time for Congress to take it to the finish line." Appreciating Mr Ogebe for contacting him, he said, "I appreciate your concerns and welcome your continued feedback" and "I appreciate your views on this matter, as I do your patience as we navigate a great deal of communication."

a6500.speaker: International Rescue Committee (IRC) (statement)
a6500.speech: “Recent heavy rainfall has led to flooding, resulting in destruction of crops, loss of livestock and displacement. Swarms of multiplying desert locusts have also been destroying pastures and crops, leading to further food insecurity. Some areas are recording admissions for severe acute malnutrition at 50% higher than for the same period last year. A massive twelve fold increase in Covid-19 cases between June and September is further compounding needs as families have been unable to obtain income or access food due to movement restrictions” ; the statement further said that IRC is working to safeguard the lives of affected and at-risk communities from the COVID-19 pandemic by raising community awareness on COVID-19 risk factors, providing personal protective equipment, and building and installing water points, and that “the IRC is assisting desert locust and flood-affected households with multi-purpose cash transfer and non-food items to fill food security gaps and provide relief.”

a6500.speaker: Frank McManus, IRC Ethiopia Country Director
a6500.speech: “The multiple issues of flooding, locusts, intercommunal violence and COVID-19 are highly concerning given the already massive humanitarian needs in the country. The slowdown of the economy and lockdown restrictions mean that people have not been able to access income and there is an upward pressure on food prices” ; “Over 19 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance in Ethiopia. At four times the number of people displaced in 2019, as a result of the flooding, more than 300,000 people have been displaced in 2020 and have had their homes and livelihoods lost or damaged. A total of over 1 million people have been adversely affected by the floods overall. With the spread of COVID-19, people that have been displaced are amongst the most vulnerable due to the often congested living space, compromised health conditions, and inadequate access to basic services. The IRC is providing essential support through distributions of non-food items, including emergency shelter, household goods, hygiene kits, and cash assistance to over 36,500 affected people” ; “Despite the IRC’s work, the unmet humanitarian needs are still great. With more funding for our work, we will be able to reach even more people with the critical support they so desperately need after losing their homes and livelihoods.”

a6579.speaker: United Nations
a6579.speech: Warned that as many as 630 000 people could be in need of help following the massive flooding in Myanmar in the wake of Typhoon Yagi.

a6579.speaker: Official figures
a6579.speech: Show that the floods and landslides triggered by Yagi across northern Vietnam, Laos, Thailand and Myanmar have killed more than 500 people.

a6579.speaker: State TV in junta-ruled Myanmar
a6579.speech: Confirmed 226 fatalities late on Monday, with 77 people still missing, doubling the previous toll of 113 ; said that nearly 260 000 hectares of rice paddies and other crops had been destroyed by floods.

a6579.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA)
a6579.speech: Said an estimated 631 000 people had been affected by flooding across Myanmar ; said food, drinking water, shelter and clothes are all urgently needed, warning that downed communication lines, blocked roads and damaged bridges were all severely hampering relief efforts ; said more resources are urgently needed.

a6579.speaker: IOM - UN Migration (@UNmigration), social media post
a6579.speech: "#TyphoonYagi left massive displacements and destruction in #VietNam affecting over 74,000 families. IOM is on the ground supporting the government's humanitarian and recovery efforts. We need #ClimateAction now to prevent further displacement. #ClimateMigration."

a6579.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme
a6579.speech: Said on Monday that the floods were the worst in Myanmar's recent history, without giving precise details.

a6579.speaker: Myanmar junta
a6579.speech: Issued a rare appeal for foreign aid at the weekend, with neighbour India so far the only country to respond, sending 10 tonnes of materials including dry rations, clothing and medicine.

a6579.speaker: Special Advisory Council for Myanmar (@SpecialCouncil), social media post
a6579.speech: "An international humanitarian response to #TyphoonYagi is needed urgently in #Myanmar. States bordering must open their borders to allow int'l aid to reach the Myanmar people through existing resistance authority & civil society networks."

a6579.speaker: Vietnamese authorities
a6579.speech: Report that in Vietnam the death toll stands at 292, with 38 missing, more than 230 000 homes damaged and 280 000 hectares of crops destroyed.

a6579.speaker: Vietnamese state media, citing an initial government assessment
a6579.speech: Reported that the typhoon caused an estimated 40 trillion dong ($1.6 billion) in economic losses.

a6671.speaker: Amartya Sen, economist
a6671.speech: As Amartya Sen reminded us many years ago, famines are a reflection of policy deficits—in this case, the management of the Somali crisis and absence of long term planning vis-a-vis this delicate ecosystem.

a6671.speaker: Giulio Tremonti, Italian Finance Minister
a6671.speech: Reportedly said that on a sinking Titanic it does not matter whether you are sitting in first class or economy.

a6671.speaker: David Cameron, UK Prime Minister
a6671.speech: On his recent visit to South Africa, Prime Minister David Cameron observed that an African free trade area would increase Africa's GDP per annum by 62 billion dollars, 20 billion more than combined ODA.

a6711.speaker: Olasupo Shasore (SAN), Senior Partner at ALP Nigeria
a6711.speech: Described the partnership as a major step forward for the group's clients and operations across Africa: "Getting one of the most highly regarded lawyers in Francophone Africa, Serge Effi, and his firm, Effi & Associes, to join the ALPi Practice Group is fantastic news for us and for our clients, including those across the ten African Union member states where we now operate." ; added that the bilingual strength and cross-border expertise of Effi & Associes would enhance the network's capacity to serve clients across both civil and common law systems: "This step advances our commitment to building a truly Pan-African legal services platform designed for the AfCFTA era, and for truly opening up African business."

a6711.speaker: Gabby Asare Otchere-Darko, Senior Partner of Africa Legal Associates (ALP Ghana)
a6711.speech: Said the inclusion of Effi & Associes reflected ALPi's deliberate strategy to establish a strong presence across Africa's major economic zones: "Africa is becoming increasingly a single market, where we see our clients, from multinationals to SMEs, expanding across borders. That's why we are deliberate about ensuring that ALPi has a presence across the continent for our clients and potential partners both within Africa and globally. Having Effi & Associes as part of the family perfectly aligns with our vision to build a one-stop, high-quality advisory firm for clients seeking to do or expand their business in Africa."

a6711.speaker: Dr Serge Effi, Managing Partner of Effi & Associes
a6711.speech: Said joining ALPi represented an exciting opportunity to offer seamless legal services to clients across Africa's evolving business landscape: "We are very happy to be part of this Pan-African-focused law family. This partnership is greatly welcomed by our clients, and it enhances our ability to offer seamless legal services across both civil law and common law jurisdictions. This is exactly where Africa is going, which is toward deeper integration and cooperation among its professionals and markets. We are excited to represent ALPi in Cote d'Ivoire."

a6711.speaker: Uyi Giwa-Osagie, Partner at ALP Nigeria
a6711.speech: Added that the partnership would further strengthen business and trade relations between Nigeria and Cote d'Ivoire, two of the fastest-growing economies in West Africa.

a6780.speaker: Matshidiso Moeti, WHO Regional Director for Africa
a6780.speech: Speaking at a virtual seminar, said emergency response efforts were being ramped up to provide relief to communities affected by Cyclone Freddy: "While we work to understand the full extent of the devastation, our priority is to ensure that affected communities and families receive health assistance for immediate needs as well as to limit the risks of water-borne diseases and other infections spreading."

a6780.speaker: Matshidiso Moeti, WHO Regional Director for Africa
a6780.speech: "With the rise in climate-related health emergencies in Africa, it's clear that more needs to be done to bolster preparedness for climatic hazards, so that communities can better cope with the impacts of the devastating natural disasters."

a6780.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO estimates)
a6780.speech: Estimated that more than 1.4 million people in Mozambique, Malawi and Madagascar were affected by Cyclone Freddy, and that it "stretched the capacity of health facilities to the limit. Houses, schools, roads and other infrastructure have been destroyed or damaged, and swathes of farmland inundated".

a6903.speaker: Anthony Ohemeng-Boamah, UNDP Liberia Resident Representative (Op-Ed, 20 November 2024, “Liberia: A pitstop along the journey at COP 29”)
a6903.speech: Expounded on how his organization supported the country’s participation in this year’s climate change forum, COP29; said UNDP supported Liberia’s pre-COP event that brought together national and local leaders, civil society, youth and women representatives, and other stakeholders to explore key political aspects of negotiations, find solutions to outstanding issues, and set the tone for the country’s participation ; Said the organization supports the participation of eight national stakeholders on the Liberian delegation at COP29, including key negotiators from EPA, the Forestry Development Authority (FDA), the National Disaster Management Agency, and representatives from the Federation of Liberian Youth and Civil Society ; “Recognizing youth as over half of Liberia’s population, UNDP collaborated with the Liberia Youth for Climate Action and the Government of Liberia to host a side event on 14 November, highlighting challenges, best practices, and lessons learned to enable broad-based and inclusive youth participation in the revision of NDC 3.0.” ; According to him, the side event explored promoting policy change, leveraging current and emerging youth empowerment opportunities, mapping existing financial mechanisms, identifying key stakeholders and financial institutions, and connecting youth-led initiatives to NDC targets.

a6903.speaker: Anthony Ohemeng-Boamah, UNDP Liberia Resident Representative (Op-Ed)
a6903.speech: “At the Conference of the Parties-COP29 in Baku, Azerbaijan, global climate negotiations reached a critical juncture. Temperature records are being breached, and climate impacts are more widespread and devastatingly intertwined with other crises on biodiversity, food, finance, and increasing global conflicts. Along Liberia’s coast, communities are being devastated by erosion and floods, and key agricultural regions are shattered by irregular temperatures and rain patterns. The world must take rapid, sustained, and large-scale action to limit global warming.” ; “UNDP will coordinate UN System-wide support for NDC preparations… UNDP will facilitate a post-COP29 national report and dialogue to take stock of the Baku negotiations and reflect on key takeaways and opportunities for Liberia.” ; “UNDP is implementing projects that directly support Liberia’s national goals and global climate commitments by working in partnership with other UN Agencies, the European Union, the governments of Sweden, the United Kingdom, and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), among others… UNDP has supported the government in mobilizing climate finance valued at approximately $30 million in the last 5 years, for the Monrovia Metropolitan Coastal Resilient Project and the Sinoe Coastal Project.”

a6903.speaker: Anthony Ohemeng-Boamah, UNDP Liberia Resident Representative (Op-Ed, “A Call to Action”)
a6903.speech: “Liberia can transform climate challenges into sustainable growth opportunities. To do that, the Liberian Government must take bold leadership and align national policies with climate priorities. It must also create an enabling environment for climate finance… Development partners should encourage and enable the government of Liberia by providing financial resources, and technical expertise, and building local capacity for climate programs… The Private Sector must also engage by unlocking green infrastructure investments… Civil Society should continue to increase advocacy for climate justice, ensure equitable financing, prioritize community-driven solutions, and guarantee locally-owned climate action plans. UNDP reiterates its commitment to supporting Liberia in building capacities and implementing programs to fully unlock the potential of a green economy for the country. Together, we can help Liberia strengthen climate resilience, and seize opportunities for a sustainable future while ensuring no one is left behind.”

a6903.speaker: Jeremiah Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a6903.speech: Addressed world leaders at the COP29 climate summit emphasizing the importance of the Loss and Damages Fund ; Informed the Summit that Liberia will further increase its climate ambition at the time of the country’s third generation NDC, considering biodiversity protection, conservation of mangroves, freshwater ecosystem services, child rights, and human mobility ; He advocated for stronger cooperative actions and decisions on Articles 6.2, 6.4, and 6.8 at COP29 consistent with the Africa Group’s position in operationalizing carbon-market and non-carbon market mechanisms.

a6903.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the Environment Protection Agency (EPA)
a6903.speech: Leading the Liberian delegation side event on 16 November, announced that Liberia intends to engage in the global carbon market; harnessing carbon trading initiatives could benefit local communities and support essential national development goals, including the expansion of renewable energy and road infrastructure critical to the country’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

a6903.speaker: Liberia’s 2021 NDC Financing Strategy
a6903.speech: In its 2021 NDC Financing Strategy, Liberia estimated $490 million to achieve its climate and green growth ambitions through 2025. However, Liberia faces a funding gap of $460 million, including zero from the private sector.

a6982.speaker: Joao Matlombe, Minister of Transport and Logistics of Mozambique
a6982.speech: After visiting the company Rede Viaria de Mocambique - REVIMO on Monday morning, announced the resumption of toll collections on 15 May this year.

a6982.speaker: Joao Matlombe, Minister of Transport and Logistics of Mozambique
a6982.speech: Says that the modern infrastructure inaugurated today was designed to bring improvements to the services provided to the public with less bureaucracy, making it possible to combat corruption and poor management.

a6982.speaker: Constantino, economist, and Osvaldo Maute, businessman (interviewed by TVM)
a6982.speech: Believe that trade without restrictions on opening hours will increase earnings in the sector and increase the supply of jobs ; warn of the need to intensify inspection to guarantee respect for labour rights.

a6982.speaker: Economic operators / businessmen in Niassa province
a6982.speech: Say that the degradation of access roads, poor performance of traffic regulation agents and the high cost of cement undermine the good business environment in the province.

a6982.speaker: Semi-collective passenger transporters ("chapeiros") of Inhambane city
a6982.speech: Halting activity in protest at inspection by the municipal council, say there is excessive bureaucracy from the transport department for the licensing of the public service.

a6982.speaker: Officials and sports figures
a6982.speech: Consider that coach Miguel Guambe's new work is a great contribution to the day-to-day management of sports teams, and hope that it will be properly used.

a6982.speaker: Workers in the city of Maputo
a6982.speech: Say it is challenging to work on a public holiday, to guarantee their daily bread, on the occasion of International Workers' Day.

a6982.speaker: Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action of Mozambique
a6982.speech: Says that the growing labour conflicts are consequences of the current economic situation the country is going through.

a6982.speaker: Association of Small and Medium Enterprises of Mozambique
a6982.speech: Points with satisfaction to the gradual resumption of activities by some companies.

a7276.speaker: Selma Pallas-Musavyi, Namibia's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade
a7276.speech: Said in Havana on Monday that Namibia and Cuba want to strengthen trade and economic cooperation between the two countries in view of the "current global environment, which is marked by geopolitical tensions, a weakening multilateralism and increasing protectionism" ; called on the technical experts taking part in the meeting to act innovatively and strategically in order to promote mutual trade and investment.

a7276.speaker: Selma Pallas-Musavyi, Namibia's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade
a7276.speech: Referring to the historical relationship and the military assistance given by Cuba during the liberation struggle, said "from Cassinga to Cuito Cuanavale our countries are bound by an eternal friendship that was written (sealed) with the blood of our heroes."

a7276.speaker: Oscar Perez-Oliva Fraga, Cuban Minister (Namibia's counterpart)
a7276.speech: Emphasised that around 1,300 Namibians have been trained in Cuba and that close to 130 Cuban experts have supported the country since Namibia's independence, above all in the field of medicine.

a7276.speaker: OEC-World (online trade data platform)
a7276.speech: According to OEC-World, in 2023 Cuba exported goods worth 21 US dollars to Namibia, mainly integrated circuits (computer chips), and over the past five years exports from Cuba to Namibia have fallen by 74.6 percent annually, from 19,900 US dollars in 2018 to a mere 21 US dollars in 2023.
